tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__roam__create_block
tools.description:
Create blocks from markdown content. Target by parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage (page created if needed). Use nestUnder to insert under a specific child block. Supports nested bulleted lists via markdown indentation.

IMPORTANT: unless you've already called get_graph_guidelines for the target graph this session, call it before using this tool — including for reads. The user's conventions change how to interpret and present results, not just how to write.

Preference: Direct graph mutation. For append-only child blocks where you want Roam-side target visibility first, prefer propose_write_batch (or propose_write for a single branch).

parentUid.description: UID of parent block or page. Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

pageTitle.description: Page title to create block under (creates the page if it doesn't exist). Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

dailyNotePage.description: Target a daily note page, creating it if needed. Either a date in MM-DD-YYYY format (e.g. '03-17-2026') or a relative day: 'today', 'yesterday', or 'tomorrow' (case-insensitive; resolved to the user's local calendar date). Exactly one of parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage is required.

If no match exists, creates a new child block with this text first, then inserts under it. Works with parentUid, pageTitle, or dailyNotePage.

Show remaining content verbatim, never paraphrase. Use maxDepth for large blocks.

  - This was written with OpenSpec, but because there are many pending decisions, we decided to stay at a pre-spec level. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>
- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT"/>
    - One pseudo-user per space, with a shared space password stored in the platform settings. Every graph member can read that password. <roam uid="kb_Gd_svI"/>
    - One pseudo-user per group. <roam uid="IH0tyDi5Z"/>
    - The `everyone` pseudo-user for public content (ENG-1837 branch, not merged). <roam uid="oJCpZSrsO"/>
    - Agent users for read-only agent access (planned in the `agent-read-only-access` OpenSpec change). <roam uid="viJKLrjcB"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Decision: how a personal account is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>
    - Option 2: reach scoped by attestation. Preferred so far. <roam uid="bpN-mO9lF"/>
      - The claim record holds the person, the `PlatformAccount`, the vouching space (the space whose session made the claim), and the attestation level. <roam uid="2GK3rGpKk"/>
      - An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space. <roam uid="28rjLezNq"/>
      - A `corroborated` or `attested` claim gives access in every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="qmd_UoR4o"/>
      - A forged assertion stays in a space whose password the forger already holds, so it gains nothing. <roam uid="mSMyEGsZg"/>
      - Proving identity later widens the reach in place, with no new kind of record. <roam uid="yb6-e7E5i"/>
      - Cost: with weakly proven claims, the person connects each space once. <roam uid="YiPQJDhje"/>
      - Cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="9M61pEmt1"/>
  - Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
    - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
    - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
    - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. The agent access design notes the same cost. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
    - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
    - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
    - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
    - Agent grants: the same pattern inside `my_user_accounts()` as `agent_grant`, but a different table. An agent has exactly one principal and is gated by its role claim. An agent owned by a person adds one level: agent, person, space, group. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>
  - Prerequisite <roam uid="huOP3R6up"/>
    - The `group_membership` insert hole is closed first (see Constraints). It lets any caller join a uid that has no members, and space pseudo-users have none, so it already exposes spaces today (found by reading the policy, not tested). <roam uid="EogAwWnXT"/>
- Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5"/>
  - **Why it matters:** every access policy calls these functions, so they set what each caller reaches and add to the cost of every query. Most of this section is agreed; only the lease length is open. <roam uid="mcAP4xcAU"/>
  - Where the claim lives, without a new table <roam uid="Cq8Z7k1_K"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account`: the person who claimed the account (exists today). <roam uid="HI27RxILB"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.claim_attestation`: asserted, corroborated, attested, or frozen. <roam uid="LpZMlh92m"/>
    - `LocalAccess.vouched`: this space's session made the claim. <roam uid="Aw4Af4gJG"/>
    - `LocalAccess.last_seen`: the lease. <roam uid="vZYlXEL7h"/>
    - `LocalAccess` admin level and delegated flag: the space-admin decision. <roam uid="p3wczF1ke"/>
    - Each space's pseudo-user uid is needed. Today it is found through the anonymous `PlatformAccount`, whose `account_local_id` is `get_space_anonymous_email(platform, id)`. A `Space.principal_uid` column would be clearer. <roam uid="IRNBzF_Oa"/>
  - Three nested sets of uids for a caller <roam uid="mEKDhdnT_"/>
    - `self_to_spaces()`: the caller, plus the spaces the caller acts for through claims (reach rule, lease, not frozen). <roam uid="9DQlyb6HQ"/>
    - `self_to_groups()`: that, plus the groups of every uid in it. One pass over `group_membership`, no recursion. <roam uid="xgb-TmzcC"/>
    - `self_to_everyone()`: that, plus the `everyone` pseudo-user. Replaces `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="p_XEWf7L1"/>
    - These replace `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. Outside SQL, both names only appear in the generated `dbTypes.ts`. <roam uid="25IooWjth"/>
  - Which set each check uses <roam uid="bZ325OCEt"/>
    - Membership and admin checks on a group use `self_to_spaces()`. Groups don't count, otherwise membership would nest. `everyone` never counts. <roam uid="V3mJeIE0I"/>
    - Checks for sharing a space with an account use `self_to_groups()`. A public grant must not count as sharing. <roam uid="_xnlnN4_m"/>
    - Reads use `self_to_everyone()`. <roam uid="XOZ7nL4S6"/>
  - Each set is computed for one principal and works for any caller <roam uid="-7GZXBiOr"/>
    - Space session: the space and its groups, the same as today. <roam uid="INz7A6X98"/>
    - Person: the person, their direct groups, their claimed spaces, and those spaces' groups. <roam uid="9wwDV7p4T"/>
    - Agent: its own expansion, plus the full expansion of its principal from `agent_grant`. <roam uid="pul5mAdGy"/>
  - Group admin <roam uid="GNGlWJVoz"/>
    - Stage 1: `is_group_admin(G)` is true when any uid in `self_to_spaces()` is an admin of G. A person who acts for space S is an admin of G whenever S is. This lets people be promoted to direct group admins without being direct members first. <roam uid="gparhcgzS"/>
    - Stage 2: restrict the space-derived part to people who are admins of S. It waits until space admins exist. <roam uid="ziRKyT9d4"/>
    - The same rule applies to leaving a group: the `group_membership` delete policy would let a person make S leave G. Stage 2 restricts it too. <roam uid="FA4vWPAT2"/>
    - `my_pseudo_accounts` must check `self_to_spaces()` instead of `auth.uid()`. Otherwise a person never sees the groups of their spaces, and publishing to groups finds none. <roam uid="F5fgLmqoL"/>
  - Agreed <roam uid="cCtIzCldr"/>
    - Caps: the sets return each uid with a cap, as `TABLE(uid, cap)` rather than bare uids. Permission checks use the lower of the grant and the cap. A group reached through a capped space inherits the cap. The same mechanism covers read-only access through a space and read-only agents. <roam uid="vLHTviSzs"/>
    - Cost: for a person, each call walks `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `Space` and `group_membership`. That is fine once per statement but not once per row, so the RLS rewrite to the `= ANY((SELECT ...))` pattern becomes a prerequisite. <roam uid="SyoGpN9DQ"/>
  - Open: the lease length (90 days is a placeholder). <roam uid="IN5YpaEA5"/>
- Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>
  - Space admin <roam uid="3l40D2TI3"/>
    - **Why it matters:** every admin power is something any holder of the space password can do today, for example rotating that password or joining groups for the space. The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together. <roam uid="YyVfTf1I1"/>
    - Guessed: the plugin reports who is admin. <roam uid="RBdmXSvZj"/>
      - Roam: the plugin reads `roamAlphaAPI.user.isAdmin` ([developer documentation](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/U5DkRU6hr)). It is synchronous, takes no parameters, and answers only for the current user. This replaces the earlier guess, the first user page created in the graph. <roam uid="SdqDeXOxt"/>
        - The plugin can't ask about other users, so an admin is recorded only once that admin runs the plugin. Until then the space has no admin at this tier.

{"guidelines":"# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="10"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
