content.text:
{"id":"P-DIS-140","uuid":"a7b4bbc1-f729-4248-8b8b-b9bf01ab7ca7","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes","summary":"Upload a PDF to a web page and have AI extract nodes","description":"# <linear-comment id="11549f99-1c47-4faa-bcd8-0e7c97dc2afa" resolved="false">DG AI Paper Extraction — MVP-0 Scope</linear-comment>

> **Status:** Draft — Approved. 

---

1\. Goal + Non-Goals

### Goal

Standalone page on discoursegraphs.com: upload one PDF → get draft DG nodes with supporting snippets → review → select → copy to clipboard.

MVP-0 delivers one architecturally sound, mergeable, end-to-end flow. The point is not optimized extraction — it's a working flow that lets real users evaluate extraction quality, node taxonomy, and UX.

### Non-Goals

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| ✗ | Solving extraction quality in a final or optimized way. |
| ✗ | Automating publishing into Roam or Obsidian. |
| ✗ | Supporting all paper types, schemas, or edge cases. |
| ✗ | Building production-grade evaluation infrastructure. |
| ✗ | Batch processing or multi-paper upload. |
| ✗ | Relation extraction (nodes only, per [Jan 20 All Hands](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vDuO_Slg5>)). |

### Discourse Graph Context

This project is grounded in `[[FUN]]` - [Formulate research directions and experiments from conversation with / synthesis of literature](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Z1nI1LxMl>): *"The goal is to be able to annotate, capture, and reuse the key information stored in published papers."*

It targets the "taking and making notes" portion of that `FUN`. The closest existing manual precedent is `[[FLO]]` - [Make DG literature notes on a research source](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FFE29QvNt>) — Alpha status, weekly frequency, high impact. That flow involves reading a paper, pasting screenshots / writing notes, and using `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Roam)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/uILBlKlyz>) to create individual nodes manually.

**Adjacent context:**

* `[[FLO]]` - [Create citeable entry for a paper in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/ioHOXjpaT>) — upstream prereq
* `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Obsidian)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/_Gn_XBvow>) — Obsidian-side analog (less developed)
* `[[FLO]]` - [Prepare and send nodes to page for synthesis](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FHEvBk5D7>) — downstream adjacent (different FUN, but where extracted nodes eventually go)
* `[[ISS]]` - [AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/lcuLhptzE>) — the issue that spawned this project
* `[[ART]]` - [Roam DG/Discourse Graph this Page](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GvUUWUOua>) — prior art for auto-generating DG from content

**Proposed new nodes** (to be created as part of this work — not yet in graph):

* A new `FLO` for the AI-assisted extraction flow
* A new `ART` for the extraction feature on discoursegraphs.com

---

## 2. Architecture

This section defines the system design and domain boundaries for the extraction feature. MVP-0 implements a thin slice; the design should hold up as the project expands without prescribing what that expansion looks like.

### 2.1 Domain Model

| Concept | Description | MVP-0 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Paper** | An uploaded academic PDF. | Transient in MVP-0. |
| **Extraction Run** | One invocation of the pipeline against a paper with specific settings (node types, research question). | Ephemeral in MVP-0. |
| **Extracted Node** | A single extracted DG node: type tag, content, supporting snippet. | Rendered in the browser in MVP-0, copied as plain text. |
| **Evaluation** | A judgment about extraction quality on a known (paper, DG) pair. | Manual notes in Roam for MVP-0. |

### 2.2 System Layers

Three layers, each independently improvable:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Frontend Review App                                    │
│  Page on discoursegraphs.com. Handles upload,           │
│  configuration, result display, selection, and export.  │
│                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Extraction Engine: LLM                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Evaluation Layer                                       │
│  Compares extraction output against known graphs.       │
│  MVP-0: manual workflow, notes in Roam.                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The engine is the part that improves most over time. The interface between engine and frontend (the extracted node schema) should be stable even as internals change.

### 2.3 Key Design Decisions

* <linear-comment id="1fef4528-9b50-4fa6-8e0d-fb291064b1f5" resolved="true">**Extracted node schema**</linear-comment> **is the contract.** The extraction engine returns extracted-nodes in a normalized schema. The frontend consumes it. The evaluation layer compares against it. This is the seam that lets each layer evolve independently.
  * nodeType type definiton minimum:
    * label
    * definition
    * claimTag
* **The extraction engine is a pipeline, not a monolith.** pdf paper, prompt, model, and output formatter are separate concerns. MVP-0 wires them simply; any stage can be swapped later.
* **This lives inside the existing** `apps/website`. The Next.js app already has LLM API routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), Supabase integration, Tailwind, and Vercel hosting. New routes and pages follow existing patterns.

### 2.4 Architectural Constraints

* Prompt, parser/chunker(llm now), model, and formatter must be swappable without changing the frontend.
* The evaluation workflow reuses the same extracted nodes output format as the frontend.
* No multi-pass, ensemble, RL, or retrieval-refinement in MVP-0.
* No direct write-back to Roam or Obsidian.

### 2.5 M0 Deliverable

Agree on:

1. The Extracted node schema (fields, types, what the frontend expects)
2. The extraction request/response contract (what the API route accepts and returns)
3. Confirmation that the layer boundaries above are right

---

## 3. V0 Scope

### Flow

```
Upload one PDF
  → Optionally enter a target research question
  → Review/toggle default node types before running
  → Run extraction
  → Review extracted nodes — each shows type tag + content + supporting snippet
  → Select desired blocks
  → Copy selected as plain text to clipboard
```

### In-Scope Use Cases

| ID | Description |
| -- | -- |
| UC1 | Upload a single academic paper PDF and get extracted DG nodes |
| UC2 | Optionally scope extraction to a target research question |
| UC3 | Toggle node types on/off from a default set before running |
| UC4 | Review each extracted node against its supporting snippet |
| UC5 | <linear-comment id="419d4fd7-9c92-4153-a75d-b91e57586cf3" resolved="false">Select and copy extracted node as plain text for use in </linear-comment> |
| UC6 | <linear-comment id="0990f58f-c5a2-4bd7-84ee-eafe914a4694" resolved="false">Joel and Matt manually compare extraction results against known benchmark datasets</linear-comment> (eval TBD) |

### Out of Scope

* Multiple papers / batch processing
* Custom user-defined node types
* Roam/Obsidian formatted export or direct object creation
* Image/table CDN hosting (LLM references fig/table numbers instead)
* Semantic Reader integration
* Advanced extraction (multi-pass, RL, ensemble, retrieval-augmented)
* Automated evaluation tooling or new eval-specific datastore
* Full auth or multi-user accounts

### Constraints / Assumptions

* One agreed end-to-end flow, not every possible branch.
* Default node-type set and tag labels are a **dependency on Matt/Joel**. Target types from the configured graph schema: CLM, EVD, QUE, RES, THE, Source. Exact subset to be confirmed before M1.
* Output is plain text; downstream formatting handled by user.
* Manual review is part of the product, not a fallback.
* Flow over polish; design can be simple and library-driven.
* Code must be production-worthy: clear boundaries, maintainable, mergeable to main.
* MVP-0 must only affect opted-in users and must not modify existing data.
* Security: LLM keys server-side on Vercel. Hard spending cap, spending alerts, easy key revocation. No shared user datastore. Worst case = token drain.
* Evaluation
  * Evaluation results will be recorded in Roam
    * user will copy and paste from the app and manually add feedback
    * can use <issue id="951383f9-b49b-4248-a7f2-e716849b2b33" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1604/extraction-run-on-benchmark-papers-quality-documented">ENG-1604</issue> 
    * can use [\[\[ISS\]\] - Initial paper benchmark results from \[\[Project/AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes\]\]](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SNeqhmSBF>)

---

## 4. Milestones

[M0: Architecture + Contracts](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-be0f7fd4-3db1-4680-8579-503ade3a900f>)

> **Deliverable:** Agreed extracted node schema, nodeType schema, PDF parser choice (LLM), and confirmation of layer boundaries. **Acceptance:** Interfaces reviewed; prompt/parser/model swappable without frontend redesign. **Dependencies:** None.

[M1: API route setup + Default Prompt](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e480b1cb-bd25-4e21-a0f8-c569806967a5>)

> **Deliverable:** API route + settings and returns normalized extracted nodes. **Acceptance:** Sample paper processed end-to-end; each extracted includes tag, content, and support reference; works on 2-3 benchmark papers; prompt includes few-shot examples. **Dependencies:** M0; node-type set from Matt/Joel; baseline prompt.

<linear-comment id="7b40b257-b525-434a-adb9-69b69a57c69b" resolved="false">[M2: Frontend App](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e8677cd6-0a74-4a87-a0c2-664b0a3d49a8>)</linear-comment>

> **Deliverable:** Page on discoursegraphs.com — upload, configure, run, review, select, copy. **Acceptance:** User completes full flow in browser; blocks render clearly; clipboard works. **Dependencies:** Stable M1 output schema.

[M3: Evaluation Baseline](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-171e0e29-3097-49b2-a508-aaa2a6785b18>)

> **Deliverable:** Manual evaluation — extraction run on benchmark papers, quality documented. **Acceptance:** Joel and Matt each evaluate 2-3 papers against known graphs; observations in Roam; obvious quality gaps identified. **Dependencies:** M1 stable; benchmark papers available.

### [M4: Smoke Test + Review + Merge ](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-8aca861c-37fa-4607-b2cd-93cd867b41cf>)

> **Deliverable:** Team review of full flow, decision log, merge to main. **Acceptance:** 10-min smoke test; axis-specific feedback on extraction quality, taxonomy, UX; merged and accessible. **Dependencies:** M2, M3.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### P0 — Must have

FR0 - <issue id="9b44a383-68ca-463a-b097-764223f6072a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1601">ENG-1601</issue>

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| FR1 | <issue id="287e58ad-2246-4484-ac8d-5f28f603325a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1592">ENG-1592</issue> |
| FR2 | <issue id="171b2065-a196-4c0f-8487-26215b8a4921" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1593">ENG-1593</issue> |
| FR3 | <issue id="ea927329-04f6-4a02-9bcb-fd88031cd343" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1594">ENG-1594</issue> |
| FR4 | <issue id="e04c6495-d75c-42a8-af3d-d08959155e1d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1602/api-to-send-uploaded-pdf-to-chosen-llms-to-parse-from-fr1">ENG-1602</issue>, uses FR6 prompt |
| FR5 | ~~Chunk by section where boundaries are detectable (Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion)~~ using llm parser, will be included in FR6 prompt |
| FR6 | <issue id="089a3b0d-2d3e-42f8-b1a4-117b137fc3c6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1595">ENG-1595</issue> |
| FR7 | Each extracted node includes: node type tag, node content, supporting quote or figure/table reference |
| FR8 | <issue id="7829f53b-e3c4-4e62-81b9-668b52be05c8" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1596">ENG-1596</issue> |
| FR9 | <issue id="675ea294-3530-40e0-bfd4-aed017be1037" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1597">ENG-1597</issue> |
| FR10 | <issue id="d2fb1278-5075-424e-b13f-1e44cc23fe01" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1598">ENG-1598</issue> |

### 5.5  Non-Functional

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| NFR1 | <linear-comment id="592cad65-4129-4ab8-9a06-301ac26221f6" resolved="true">Support references include enough location info for quick re-finding in the paper</linear-comment> |
| NFR2 | <linear-comment id="26d54b85-b754-4d37-8d5c-ef96c94c610b" resolved="true">Reasonable defaults so a first-time user completes the flow without setup</linear-comment> |

---

## 6. Open Questions + Risks

### Open Questions

| \# | Question |
| -- | -- |
| 2 | <linear-comment id="ec7498b7-673d-485a-89d2-bc9671281e34" resolved="true">What does the clipboard output format look like? Should it match the graph's `[[CLM]] - {content}` format?</linear-comment> |
| 3 | Which few-shot examples should the prompt include, and from which papers? |
| 4 | What size or runtime limits on uploaded PDFs? |
| 5 | LLM model choice for extraction — cost vs. quality vs. context window? |
| 6 | Should the new `FLO` and `ART` discourse nodes be created before or after M0? |
| 7 | <linear-comment id="f6dd60e1-5543-463e-9194-713966bd8f0d" resolved="true">What fields belong in the extracted node schema to support future persistence without over-engineering MVP-0?</linear-comment> |

### Risks

| Risk | Impact |
| -- | -- |
| PDF extraction quality varies across publishers and scan quality | Weak input → weak extracted nodes |
| Figure/table-heavy papers may produce weak support references | Poor verifiability for certain paper types |
| Single broad prompt may over- or under-extract depending on paper structure | Inconsistent output quality |
| Public endpoint introduces token-abuse risk if spending limits are too loose | Cost blowout |
| If the review UI doesn't make verification easy, feedback quality will be poor even if extraction is reasonable | Team learning bottleneck |
| LLM PDF extraction might be a black box | Unable to inspect what text/content was actually extracted |
| LLM PDF extraction uses vision model | Which costs more |

---

{"id":"P-DIS-140","uuid":"a7b4bbc1-f729-4248-8b8b-b9bf01ab7ca7","icon":null,"color":"#bec2c8","name":"AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes","summary":"Upload a PDF to a web page and have AI extract nodes","description":"# <linear-comment id="11549f99-1c47-4faa-bcd8-0e7c97dc2afa" resolved="false">DG AI Paper Extraction — MVP-0 Scope</linear-comment>

> **Status:** Draft — Approved. 

---

1\. Goal + Non-Goals

### Goal

Standalone page on discoursegraphs.com: upload one PDF → get draft DG nodes with supporting snippets → review → select → copy to clipboard.

MVP-0 delivers one architecturally sound, mergeable, end-to-end flow. The point is not optimized extraction — it's a working flow that lets real users evaluate extraction quality, node taxonomy, and UX.

### Non-Goals

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| ✗ | Solving extraction quality in a final or optimized way. |
| ✗ | Automating publishing into Roam or Obsidian. |
| ✗ | Supporting all paper types, schemas, or edge cases. |
| ✗ | Building production-grade evaluation infrastructure. |
| ✗ | Batch processing or multi-paper upload. |
| ✗ | Relation extraction (nodes only, per [Jan 20 All Hands](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/vDuO_Slg5>)). |

### Discourse Graph Context

This project is grounded in `[[FUN]]` - [Formulate research directions and experiments from conversation with / synthesis of literature](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/Z1nI1LxMl>): *"The goal is to be able to annotate, capture, and reuse the key information stored in published papers."*

It targets the "taking and making notes" portion of that `FUN`. The closest existing manual precedent is `[[FLO]]` - [Make DG literature notes on a research source](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FFE29QvNt>) — Alpha status, weekly frequency, high impact. That flow involves reading a paper, pasting screenshots / writing notes, and using `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Roam)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/uILBlKlyz>) to create individual nodes manually.

**Adjacent context:**

* `[[FLO]]` - [Create citeable entry for a paper in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/ioHOXjpaT>) — upstream prereq
* `[[FLO]]` - [Create DG node (Obsidian)](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/_Gn_XBvow>) — Obsidian-side analog (less developed)
* `[[FLO]]` - [Prepare and send nodes to page for synthesis](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/FHEvBk5D7>) — downstream adjacent (different FUN, but where extracted nodes eventually go)
* `[[ISS]]` - [AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/lcuLhptzE>) — the issue that spawned this project
* `[[ART]]` - [Roam DG/Discourse Graph this Page](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GvUUWUOua>) — prior art for auto-generating DG from content

**Proposed new nodes** (to be created as part of this work — not yet in graph):

* A new `FLO` for the AI-assisted extraction flow
* A new `ART` for the extraction feature on discoursegraphs.com

---

## 2. Architecture

This section defines the system design and domain boundaries for the extraction feature. MVP-0 implements a thin slice; the design should hold up as the project expands without prescribing what that expansion looks like.

### 2.1 Domain Model

| Concept | Description | MVP-0 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Paper** | An uploaded academic PDF. | Transient in MVP-0. |
| **Extraction Run** | One invocation of the pipeline against a paper with specific settings (node types, research question). | Ephemeral in MVP-0. |
| **Extracted Node** | A single extracted DG node: type tag, content, supporting snippet. | Rendered in the browser in MVP-0, copied as plain text. |
| **Evaluation** | A judgment about extraction quality on a known (paper, DG) pair. | Manual notes in Roam for MVP-0. |

### 2.2 System Layers

Three layers, each independently improvable:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Frontend Review App                                    │
│  Page on discoursegraphs.com. Handles upload,           │
│  configuration, result display, selection, and export.  │
│                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Extraction Engine: LLM                                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Evaluation Layer                                       │
│  Compares extraction output against known graphs.       │
│  MVP-0: manual workflow, notes in Roam.                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The engine is the part that improves most over time. The interface between engine and frontend (the extracted node schema) should be stable even as internals change.

### 2.3 Key Design Decisions

* <linear-comment id="1fef4528-9b50-4fa6-8e0d-fb291064b1f5" resolved="true">**Extracted node schema**</linear-comment> **is the contract.** The extraction engine returns extracted-nodes in a normalized schema. The frontend consumes it. The evaluation layer compares against it. This is the seam that lets each layer evolve independently.
  * nodeType type definiton minimum:
    * label
    * definition
    * claimTag
* **The extraction engine is a pipeline, not a monolith.** pdf paper, prompt, model, and output formatter are separate concerns. MVP-0 wires them simply; any stage can be swapped later.
* **This lives inside the existing** `apps/website`. The Next.js app already has LLM API routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), Supabase integration, Tailwind, and Vercel hosting. New routes and pages follow existing patterns.

### 2.4 Architectural Constraints

* Prompt, parser/chunker(llm now), model, and formatter must be swappable without changing the frontend.
* The evaluation workflow reuses the same extracted nodes output format as the frontend.
* No multi-pass, ensemble, RL, or retrieval-refinement in MVP-0.
* No direct write-back to Roam or Obsidian.

### 2.5 M0 Deliverable

Agree on:

1. The Extracted node schema (fields, types, what the frontend expects)
2. The extraction request/response contract (what the API route accepts and returns)
3. Confirmation that the layer boundaries above are right

---

## 3. V0 Scope

### Flow

```
Upload one PDF
  → Optionally enter a target research question
  → Review/toggle default node types before running
  → Run extraction
  → Review extracted nodes — each shows type tag + content + supporting snippet
  → Select desired blocks
  → Copy selected as plain text to clipboard
```

### In-Scope Use Cases

| ID | Description |
| -- | -- |
| UC1 | Upload a single academic paper PDF and get extracted DG nodes |
| UC2 | Optionally scope extraction to a target research question |
| UC3 | Toggle node types on/off from a default set before running |
| UC4 | Review each extracted node against its supporting snippet |
| UC5 | <linear-comment id="419d4fd7-9c92-4153-a75d-b91e57586cf3" resolved="false">Select and copy extracted node as plain text for use in </linear-comment> |
| UC6 | <linear-comment id="0990f58f-c5a2-4bd7-84ee-eafe914a4694" resolved="false">Joel and Matt manually compare extraction results against known benchmark datasets</linear-comment> (eval TBD) |

### Out of Scope

* Multiple papers / batch processing
* Custom user-defined node types
* Roam/Obsidian formatted export or direct object creation
* Image/table CDN hosting (LLM references fig/table numbers instead)
* Semantic Reader integration
* Advanced extraction (multi-pass, RL, ensemble, retrieval-augmented)
* Automated evaluation tooling or new eval-specific datastore
* Full auth or multi-user accounts

### Constraints / Assumptions

* One agreed end-to-end flow, not every possible branch.
* Default node-type set and tag labels are a **dependency on Matt/Joel**. Target types from the configured graph schema: CLM, EVD, QUE, RES, THE, Source. Exact subset to be confirmed before M1.
* Output is plain text; downstream formatting handled by user.
* Manual review is part of the product, not a fallback.
* Flow over polish; design can be simple and library-driven.
* Code must be production-worthy: clear boundaries, maintainable, mergeable to main.
* MVP-0 must only affect opted-in users and must not modify existing data.
* Security: LLM keys server-side on Vercel. Hard spending cap, spending alerts, easy key revocation. No shared user datastore. Worst case = token drain.
* Evaluation
  * Evaluation results will be recorded in Roam
    * user will copy and paste from the app and manually add feedback
    * can use <issue id="951383f9-b49b-4248-a7f2-e716849b2b33" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1604/extraction-run-on-benchmark-papers-quality-documented">ENG-1604</issue> 
    * can use [\[\[ISS\]\] - Initial paper benchmark results from \[\[Project/AI-assisted extraction of DG nodes\]\]](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/SNeqhmSBF>)

---

## 4. Milestones

[M0: Architecture + Contracts](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-be0f7fd4-3db1-4680-8579-503ade3a900f>)

> **Deliverable:** Agreed extracted node schema, nodeType schema, PDF parser choice (LLM), and confirmation of layer boundaries. **Acceptance:** Interfaces reviewed; prompt/parser/model swappable without frontend redesign. **Dependencies:** None.

[M1: API route setup + Default Prompt](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e480b1cb-bd25-4e21-a0f8-c569806967a5>)

> **Deliverable:** API route + settings and returns normalized extracted nodes. **Acceptance:** Sample paper processed end-to-end; each extracted includes tag, content, and support reference; works on 2-3 benchmark papers; prompt includes few-shot examples. **Dependencies:** M0; node-type set from Matt/Joel; baseline prompt.

<linear-comment id="7b40b257-b525-434a-adb9-69b69a57c69b" resolved="false">[M2: Frontend App](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-e8677cd6-0a74-4a87-a0c2-664b0a3d49a8>)</linear-comment>

> **Deliverable:** Page on discoursegraphs.com — upload, configure, run, review, select, copy. **Acceptance:** User completes full flow in browser; blocks render clearly; clipboard works. **Dependencies:** Stable M1 output schema.

[M3: Evaluation Baseline](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-171e0e29-3097-49b2-a508-aaa2a6785b18>)

> **Deliverable:** Manual evaluation — extraction run on benchmark papers, quality documented. **Acceptance:** Joel and Matt each evaluate 2-3 papers against known graphs; observations in Roam; obvious quality gaps identified. **Dependencies:** M1 stable; benchmark papers available.

### [M4: Smoke Test + Review + Merge ](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/project/ai-assisted-extraction-of-dg-nodes-9e5aafbef2f6/overview#milestone-8aca861c-37fa-4607-b2cd-93cd867b41cf>)

> **Deliverable:** Team review of full flow, decision log, merge to main. **Acceptance:** 10-min smoke test; axis-specific feedback on extraction quality, taxonomy, UX; merged and accessible. **Dependencies:** M2, M3.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### P0 — Must have

FR0 - <issue id="9b44a383-68ca-463a-b097-764223f6072a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1601">ENG-1601</issue>

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| FR1 | <issue id="287e58ad-2246-4484-ac8d-5f28f603325a" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1592">ENG-1592</issue> |
| FR2 | <issue id="171b2065-a196-4c0f-8487-26215b8a4921" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1593">ENG-1593</issue> |
| FR3 | <issue id="ea927329-04f6-4a02-9bcb-fd88031cd343" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1594">ENG-1594</issue> |
| FR4 | <issue id="e04c6495-d75c-42a8-af3d-d08959155e1d" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1602/api-to-send-uploaded-pdf-to-chosen-llms-to-parse-from-fr1">ENG-1602</issue>, uses FR6 prompt |
| FR5 | ~~Chunk by section where boundaries are detectable (Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion)~~ using llm parser, will be included in FR6 prompt |
| FR6 | <issue id="089a3b0d-2d3e-42f8-b1a4-117b137fc3c6" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1595">ENG-1595</issue> |
| FR7 | Each extracted node includes: node type tag, node content, supporting quote or figure/table reference |
| FR8 | <issue id="7829f53b-e3c4-4e62-81b9-668b52be05c8" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1596">ENG-1596</issue> |
| FR9 | <issue id="675ea294-3530-40e0-bfd4-aed017be1037" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1597">ENG-1597</issue> |
| FR10 | <issue id="d2fb1278-5075-424e-b13f-1e44cc23fe01" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-1598">ENG-1598</issue> |

### 5.5  Non-Functional

| ID | Requirement |
| -- | -- |
| NFR1 | <linear-comment id="592cad65-4129-4ab8-9a06-301ac26221f6" resolved="true">Support references include enough location info for quick re-finding in the paper</linear-comment> |
| NFR2 | <linear-comment id="26d54b85-b754-4d37-8d5c-ef96c94c610b" resolved="true">Reasonable defaults so a first-time user completes the flow without setup</linear-comment> |

---

## 6. Open Questions + Risks

### Open Questions

| \# | Question |
| -- | -- |
| 2 | <linear-comment id="ec7498b7-673d-485a-89d2-bc9671281e34" resolved="true">What does the clipboard output format look like? Should it match the graph's `[[CLM]] - {content}` format?</linear-comment> |
| 3 | Which few-shot examples should the prompt include, and from which papers? |
| 4 | What size or runtime limits on uploaded PDFs? |
| 5 | LLM model choice for extraction — cost vs. quality vs. context window? |
| 6 | Should the new `FLO` and `ART` discourse nodes be created before or after M0? |
| 7 | <linear-comment id="f6dd60e1-5543-463e-9194-713966bd8f0d" resolved="true">What fields belong in the extracted node schema to support future persistence without over-engineering MVP-0?</linear-comment> |

### Risks

| Risk | Impact |
| -- | -- |
| PDF extraction quality varies across publishers and scan quality | Weak input → weak extracted nodes |
| Figure/table-heavy papers may produce weak support references | Poor verifiability for certain paper types |
| Single broad prompt may over- or under-extract depending on paper structure | Inconsistent output quality |
| Public endpoint introduces token-abuse risk if spending limits are too loose | Cost blowout |
| If the review UI doesn't make verification easy, feedback quality will be poor even if extraction is reasonable | Team learning bottleneck |
| LLM PDF extraction might be a black box | Unable to inspect what text/content was actually extracted |
| LLM PDF extraction uses vision model | Which costs more |

---

{"id":"P-PRO-189","uuid":"fee500c3-2209-499a-8bd5-909f666deb57","icon":null,"color":"#f7c8c1","name":"Create DG MCP function library","summary":"","description":"[View in Roam](<https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs//page/rgl9GMJe4>)

Starting with Roam:

Each ported function will be its own monorepo PR via `extensionAPI.ai.addTool` (25-tool cap per extension; per-tool scope read | append | edit).

**Status 2026-09-15: 34 functions now exist, verified, on [dg-team-mcp](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/dg-team-mcp>)** `main` **(15 discourse tools + 19 canvas tools).** The 26-function core completed with `get_candidate_nodes` (PR #14). PR #15 (<issue id="cd37120c-a0e4-4828-b77b-ab7bd1128910" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2276/canvas-mcp-nested-sub-canvas-portals-and-content-primitives">ENG-2276</issue>, merged the same day) added 8 canvas tools: tldraw-page create/rename/delete inside one canvas, nested sub-canvas portals (`canvas_add_subpage` / `canvas_link_subpage`, sharing the geo-plus-meta contract with <issue id="b0cdc4c8-3f9d-4944-a6ac-a3aa7c44b7b3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2150/nested-pages-in-tldraw-canvas">ENG-2150</issue>'s plugin PR so every deployed client still loads the board), and geo/arrow/image authoring. `canvas_move` now moves shapes between tldraw pages, and the label-bearing tools take a `size`. The prototype library lives separate from the monorepo; the remaining core work is the monorepo port itself, not yet started. The Accepted / Maybe / Backburner sections below are candidates beyond these; none have code yet except relation retraction, whose `deleteStoredRelation` primitive exists internally but is unexposed. Note that 34 is nine OVER addTool's 25-tool per-extension cap, so the consolidations proposed in the table comments are required at port time, no longer optional. The canvas_dg_add / canvas_add collapse now carries most of the reduction: it covers the eight shape-authoring tools (node, block, connect, text, frame, geo, arrow, image). The get_node + get_node_section + batch get_nodes merge and folding get_candidate_nodes into get_all_discourse_nodes recover the rest.

## Ready

| Function | What it does | Existing code | Context | Comments |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **initial** |  |  |  |  |

Starting with Roam:

Each ported function will be its own monorepo PR via `extensionAPI.ai.addTool` (25-tool cap per extension; per-tool scope read | append | edit).

**Status 2026-09-15: 34 functions now exist, verified, on [dg-team-mcp](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/dg-team-mcp>)** `main` **(15 discourse tools + 19 canvas tools).** The 26-function core completed with `get_candidate_nodes` (PR #14). PR #15 (<issue id="cd37120c-a0e4-4828-b77b-ab7bd1128910" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2276/canvas-mcp-nested-sub-canvas-portals-and-content-primitives">ENG-2276</issue>, merged the same day) added 8 canvas tools: tldraw-page create/rename/delete inside one canvas, nested sub-canvas portals (`canvas_add_subpage` / `canvas_link_subpage`, sharing the geo-plus-meta contract with <issue id="b0cdc4c8-3f9d-4944-a6ac-a3aa7c44b7b3" href="https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2150/nested-pages-in-tldraw-canvas">ENG-2150</issue>'s plugin PR so every deployed client still loads the board), and geo/arrow/image authoring. `canvas_move` now moves shapes between tldraw pages, and the label-bearing tools take a `size`. The prototype library lives separate from the monorepo; the remaining core work is the monorepo port itself, not yet started. The Accepted / Maybe / Backburner sections below are candidates beyond these; none have code yet except relation retraction, whose `deleteStoredRelation` primitive exists internally but is unexposed. Note that 34 is nine OVER addTool's 25-tool per-extension cap, so the consolidations proposed in the table comments are required at port time, no longer optional. The canvas_dg_add / canvas_add collapse now carries most of the reduction: it covers the eight shape-authoring tools (node, block, connect, text, frame, geo, arrow, image). The get_node + get_node_section + batch get_nodes merge and folding get_candidate_nodes into get_all_discourse_nodes recover the rest.

3. Ability to share link to node

content.text:
I found about 20 projects affected by DG accounts. Seven of them used the space account as a stand-in for personal accounts. My method has limits: I read every project's name and summary, searched issues for "space account" and "anonymous", and read about ten issues and projects closely. I did not go through every issue in every project.

## The accounts project itself

**Discourse Graph Accounts (P-DIS-83, Accepted)**
- The done tickets are the graph-based "Quick for Beta" path: ENG-418, 420, 423, 424, 567, 589.
- The personal-account tickets are still in Backlog: ENG-373, 405, 419, 421, 422, 918, 1511.
- **Review:** the project description and those tickets come before the Roam spec (H3a0tja8D). For example, ENG-421 assumes login happens in each frontend, but the spec leans toward login always on the Website with OAuth 2.1. Reconcile the two once the spec settles.

## Past projects that used space accounts as a workaround

**Obsidian within-lab collaboration (P-DES-133, In Progress)**
- ENG-1177 authenticates a vault as a space pseudo-user.
- ENG-1179, 1232 and 1238 build groups whose members are space pseudo-users.
- ENG-1650 is a "temporary username": it sets the name on the vault's pseudo-user and lists DG accounts as out of scope.
- ENG-2122 (Triage): if the plugin's stored password is lost, the vault loses database access, and there is no way to recover it. The ticket says a recovery path "would require DiscourseGraph accounts".
- **Review:**
  - Should the temporary username become a profile name?
  - Does ENG-2122 wait for accounts or get its own fix?
  - Do group members stay spaces?

**Sharing group management (P-ENG-170, Completed)**
- ENG-1703 opens the Website with the space's session token in the URL. The ticket says plainly that this stands in for cookie login with personal accounts.
- ENG-1702 (invite) and ENG-1723 (list members) both work on spaces.
- **Review:** this is the clearest migration case.
  - The Website login becomes personal.
  - Group admin rights would come through the `self_to_spaces()` set in the spec.
  - Decide whether you invite a person or a space.

**Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian (P-DIS-166, In Progress)**
- All publishing and importing runs under the space session.
- ENG-2298 fixed an import panel that named a Roam space after one of its authors.
- ENG-2344, 2359 and 2368 tune the `my_*` access views, which are keyed on the space identity.
- ENG-2335 checks group publication for imported nodes.
- **Review:**
  - The access views get rewritten on the `self_to_*` sets, and the RLS performance work has to be redone for them.
  - Decide how author and space names appear once profile names exist.

**KOI for knowledge interop (P-ENG-164, Backlog)**
- ENG-1837 adds the "everyone" pseudo-user.
- ENG-1674 and 1675 document the API, including space creation.
- **Review:** in the spec, `my_identity_accounts()` is to be renamed `self_to_groups()` before ENG-1837 merges. Hold the API docs until the auth model is known, or document the space flow as interim.

**Infrastructure for Embeddings (P-ENG-75, Icebox)**
- ENG-417 revised the alpha functions for the graph accounts.
- ENG-1835 ("search scoped to current space") was canceled.
- ENG-982 dealt with duplicate spaces for the browser and the desktop app.
- **Review:** low priority. Revisit search scope when semantic search comes back.

**Not checked, likely affected:**
- *Real-time tldraw collaboration (P-FEE-149, In Progress):* its scope includes "who is allowed to use real-time sync, how access is granted and revoked". I didn't check whether that relies on graph membership or on the space session.
- *Create Initial Admin Panel (P-ENG-106, Completed):* a hidden panel in the Roam settings. Worth a look to see which session it uses.

## Current or planned projects that depend on accounts

**Cross-space search**
- Projects:
  - *Search and filter nodes from other spaces in advanced node search (P-ENG-192, Planning):* it says "any space the user is a member of". Today that membership is per space, not per person.
  - *Roam: Initial advanced search (P-DIS-79):* the summary says "eventually cross graph search".
- **Review:** this is the first place a person must see how they are logged in (see the spec's UX touchpoints section). Scope P-ENG-192 so its first version doesn't hard-code space-only reach.

**Share and import to/from web (P-PRO-183, Proposal)**
- It names Discourse Graph Accounts as a requirement.

**Headless DG retrieval API and MCP from database (P-DIS-186)**
- Agents reading the database need an identity. This is the agent and agent_grant part of the spec.

**Create DG MCP function library (P-PRO-189)**
- It runs on the Roam side today and uses `tokenUserUid` for write attribution.
- "Multi-graph search" is on its backburner list and would need accounts.

**AI-assisted extraction (P-DIS-140)**
- "Full auth or multi-user accounts" is out of scope for MVP-0, and the project lists token abuse as a risk.
- Any persistence later needs accounts. The ENG-1999 audit of API route abuse is related.

**Website and inter-graph projects** (each needs either a Website login or a multi-space identity):
- DG tldraw web (P-ENG-176)
- TLdraw sync between graphs (P-DIS-153)
- Push and pull between two Roam graphs (P-DIS-165)
- Post-V0 sync architecture (P-ENG-185)

I write there directly, and only there. It maps options with costs for the group; the user does not want premature decisions, and decisions in older notes are not settled.

Decided or strong leanings, as of 2026-10-23:
- Cross-space search inside the platforms; `Website` joins the `Platform` enum; password accounts stay; no forcing Roam users to sign up; Roam API tokens need a subscription, so token-based proof is never required.
- A person reaches a space only through a claimed PlatformAccount (A, B and any direct person-to-space edge ruled out). Preferred: claim reach scoped by attestation (`asserted` reaches only the vouching space).
- No group nesting or recursive queries; no database-level invites into spaces; close the `group_membership` insert hole first.
- Space admin = flag plus level on `LocalAccess`: guessed < registered < proven, each with a delegated level just below it; delegates can name same-level delegates; demotion only of strictly lower levels, manual, through an admin UI; the delegator is not recorded. Admins approving identity claims is set aside.
- Admin can prove with a backend token, discarded or stored (stored is an explicit opt-in, and enables L6 for the whole graph).
- Emails stored but hidden until shared; names are shown as name plus PlatformAccount id. Profile visibility: one row per person and audience with an array of fields.
- Two sessions in the plugin: personal for reads, search and actions as the person; space for sync, groups and sharing. Personal session delivery: Supabase Auth as OAuth 2.1 server (plugin is a PKCE client; login always on the Website; MAU cost accepted; completing inside the plugin is nice to have, with a `secret_token` fallback). Social login is for adding identities and logging in on the Website. A claimed account shows the profile name.

- Access resolution: three nested sets `self_to_spaces()` (group membership/admin checks), `self_to_groups()` (sharing checks), `self_to_everyone()` (reads), replacing `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. A person acting for S is admin of G when S is (stage 1); stage 2 restricts that to admins of S. Sets return a cap per uid; the initplan RLS rewrite is a prerequisite.

New layer L8: Roam's Firebase ID token (IndexedDB `firebaseLocalStorageDb`, issuer `securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`, `sub` = Roam uid, verified email) can be checked server-side. Works in the desktop app and in browsers. Blocked until Roam's ToS is checked and Roam agrees.

Paper is a professional design tool for creating user interfaces. The user is working on a 2D canvas composing designs.
The Paper MCP server gives you tools to be a talented designer for web and mobile apps and websites. You can read designs from the user's file, see what the user is doing, and write HTML back into the design as new nodes.

You MUST load the full guide before other Paper tools: get_guide({ topic: "paper-mcp-instructions" }). Do this once per session; call again if a long thread may have dropped guide text.

- discourse-graph:evidence-candidates: Use when capturing findings from papers as Evidence (EVD) candidates in a discourse graph (Roam, Obsidian, or another tool). Triggers include "make / stage evd candidates", "add this paper's finding as evidence", collecting literature evidence for a question, hypothesis, claim or model, mining a paper or literature search into the graph, or sharpening vague evidence statements into specific observations. Also use when staged evidence reads like a claim, lacks a verbatim quote or figure, or loses its source on promotion.
- discourse-graph:figure-extraction: Use when a statement drawn from a paper needs the figure panel or table it reports as an image, such as grounding an evidence, claim or caveat candidate, "screenshot / crop / grab the figure", or "find the PDF for this paper". Also use when the paper's PDF may be in Zotero, in a project folder, or not on hand yet. Works in any discourse graph (Roam, Obsidian, plain markdown) and with whatever PDF and reference-manager tools are connected.

content.text:
Here's the order I'd take, with my reasons:

1. **Simplify the diagrams (your 1).** It's small, and it's the first concrete narrowing. With no separate agent principal, the identities diagram loses a login column and the agent_grant edge, and the spec text loses a section. That cut is a first step of your 2, so it opens that work.
2. **Generic to specific (your 2, first part).** This reshapes the spec. If I draft the account page or the privacy model against the generic version, I'd have to redo them once it narrows.
3. **Account management wireframe (your 3).** A static page forces concrete answers: what a person sees, where they log in, how they link a Roam or Obsidian account, and how they leave a space. It also shows where the privacy settings will live.
4. **What personal information gets published where (your 4).** The settings need a home on the page from step 3. The data side builds on the current leaning (one row per person and audience, with a list of fields), so it fits better once the page shows which fields exist.
5. **Attack slides (your 2, second part).** These go last, as you suggested. The attack steps depend on the specific login and claim flows, so slides drawn now would go stale. Once steps 2 and 3 are settled, each slide can point at a real screen or step.

One question before step 2. The spec was written to map options without deciding them. Does "specific" mean the group has now chosen, so the leanings become the design and the alternatives move to an appendix? Or does it mean keeping the options open but making each one concrete, with flows and examples instead of abstract descriptions? The two lead to different rewrites.

message.content: Oh, I wonder if we mean the same thing by "generic to specific", I was no referring to a decision! But I forgot a major point: We want to distinguish long-term vision from v0. The v0 will almost certainly not include advanced claim checking. (And using the firebase token is unlikely.) There may be intermediate steps. content.text:
Then I misread "generic to specific". What did you mean by it? My best guess is ordering the spec so it starts with the general picture and moves to the mechanics, rather than mixing levels. Tell me if that's off.

The v0 / long-term split changes my order, because it decides how everything else is laid out:

1. **Staging: accounts v0, then a ladder of steps.** v0 is personal accounts with claims only at "asserted", which reach only the vouching space. It has no advanced claim checking and no Firebase token. Each step up the ladder says what it adds, what it buys (security or functionality), and what it costs. The identity-link layers already on the page (L0 to L8) are close to the security half of that ladder; the functional half (cross-space search, Website group management, agents) needs to be lined up next to it. I'd read the page first and draft this as a new section near the top. I'd call it "accounts v0" to keep it apart from the sync v0 that already shipped.
2. **Diagrams.** Simplify for agents without a separate principal. Then decide whether v0 gets its own simpler identities diagram, with the full one kept as the vision. I suspect it should, since a v0 diagram has no attestation levels.
3. **Wireframe of v0 account management.** This makes v0 concrete: sign up, link a Roam or Obsidian account, see which spaces you reach. Later steps can show up as greyed-out or annotated additions.
4. **Personal information visibility.** Decide what v0 needs (maybe only a display name and a hidden email) and what waits.
5. **Attack slides.** These fit the ladder well: show an attack against v0, then which step closes it. That ties each step's security value to a concrete story, which may help the explanation land better than last time.

If that works for you, I'll start on 1 by reading the spec page. Those are Roam reads only; I'll ask before writing anything.

{"guidelines":"# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="11"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>
  - Understanding overall workflows <roam uid="3Qe0kZwzj" heading="3"/>
    - An observation from a pilot (Result) often triggers an idea for improvement (Issue). Issues are higher priority when they improve an important Flow, which in turn enables a key Function. Once engineering works on an issue, it becomes a feature (Artifact). <roam uid="E-6z55uoF"/>
    - Result → Issue → Flow → Function → Artifact traces the path from observation to shipped feature. <roam uid="gFNP0A0S9"/>
- Writing into the graph <roam uid="a7uWA6zlm" heading="2"/>
  - Leave node creation and tagging to the team by default (see **Agent Behavior → General rules** below). When you are explicitly asked to capture something — a candidate node, a pilot observation, a flow — follow these conventions so each block reads cleanly now **and** is trivial to promote into a formal discourse node later. <roam uid="mebOIP95I"/>
  - Put each concept in its own block <roam uid="F3EVfNmD7" heading="3"/>
    - Write one idea — one claim, observation, pain point, flow, or action — per block. Don't pack several into a single bullet. Be parsimonious with any commentary you consider adding. <roam uid="1LMq1Ui6Y"/>
      - Atomic blocks are individually addressable: each can be block-referenced (`((uid))`), tagged, and promoted to a node on its own. A compound bullet can't. <roam uid="rLZacptHP"/>
    - Use indentation to carry structure: the parent block states the idea; child blocks hold its detail, caveats, steps, and references. <roam uid="VFcltIeP4"/>
      - This mirrors a discourse node, where the title is the idea and the template sections are the children. <roam uid="dv7_tHNg5"/>
  - Make candidate blocks formalizable <roam uid="t62zcsYxS" heading="3"/>
    - When you tag a block with a candidate tag, write the statement so it can become the node's **title almost verbatim** — the eventual node title should be roughly the same words as the block. Keep it atomic and self-contained: understandable without the surrounding meeting / log context. <roam uid="QcHWU8FCu"/>
    - Match the target node's title grammar so promotion is mechanical. The candidate tags in use here are `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate` — each maps to the node type of the same prefix (see **Graph Ontology** above for every format). Common cases: <roam uid="vNFJ3JbII"/>
      - `#res-candidate` → a discrete, past-tense pilot observation → `[[RES]] - {statement} - {Source}`. Name the `@source` / UserPilot in a child so it can be appended to the title on promotion. <roam uid="Xx5QnpXMw"/>
        - Example: `Pilot users created 3x more claims after the canvas node preview shipped #res-candidate` <roam uid="8RsFzOBwL"/>
      - `#iss-candidate` → an actionable dev or research item → `[[ISS]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="0tM9FtTCr"/>
        - Example: `Group nodes on the canvas by semantic similarity #iss-candidate` <roam uid="b8CJepmiH"/>
      - `#flow-candidate` → a tool-specific interaction flow → `[[FLO]] - {statement}`. <roam uid="alG4QCDR4"/>
        - Example: `Preview / view DG node info while on the tldraw canvas #flow-candidate` <roam uid="skG-2mzeZ"/>
    - If you can't yet phrase an idea atomically, leave it as plain text and don't tag it — a vague stub can't be promoted without a rewrite. <roam uid="znTpKgzZv"/>
  - Put supporting context in child blocks <roam uid="YE6FUcUKB" heading="3"/>
    - Everything that explains, grounds, or qualifies a candidate goes in **child blocks beneath it, never crammed into the statement**.  On promotion these children carry over into the node's template sections. <roam uid="VwHNAB0ij"/>
    - `#res-candidate` → Source + method + a screenshot or Loom → **Grounding Context** and **Snippets**. `#flow-candidate` → **Description** (Goal, Loom), **Steps**, **Pain points**. `#iss-candidate` → why it matters + the Flow / Function it improves → Issue Status / Type / Project / Flow properties. <roam uid="-zzjS0GNH"/>
    - Link related nodes with `[[…]]` inside the children — those page references become the node's discourse connections (Supports / Opposes / Informs / Resolves) once it is formalized. <roam uid="pM5ojIoXO"/>
  - Reuse the existing syntax and formatting conventions <roam uid="MEWdJCUaQ" heading="3"/>
    - For how to __reference__ nodes when writing (Roam alias syntax, `((uid))`), follow **Agent Behavior → Citing and referencing nodes** below — don't paste full URLs inside Roam. <roam uid="iqnB7VJ1X"/>
    - For callouts, colors, and foldable blocks, use the palette documented in **Agent Behavior → Formatting** below. <roam uid="1-PwVXvKX"/>
    - Reference only node titles you have actually found in the graph; never fabricate one. Preserve node title regex formats exactly (`[[RES]] - … - {Source}`, `[[FLO]] - …`, `UserPilot/…`) — a malformed title silently drops the block out of the discourse graph. <roam uid="ldsx0Q1Nj"/>
- Agent Behavior <roam uid="HQkVaTtF9" heading="2"/>
  - Information hierarchy <roam uid="Omx-xxku_" heading="3"/>
    - **Prioritize formalized node pages** (full `[[TYPE]] - title` pages with templates filled in). These represent the team's vetted, structured knowledge. <roam uid="gSd5Imn_Z"/>
    - **Then candidate nodes** (`#type-candidate` tagged blocks). These are preliminary but intentionally captured ideas. <roam uid="KPWTNgy6Z"/>
    - **Then remaining content** (meeting notes, daily notes, log entries, comments). These provide context but are less curated. <roam uid="7FBUcDopw"/>
    - Rank by formality, but check authorship before you cite — only human-written blocks are citable. See **Synthesize human content, not agent content** below. <roam uid="RgZPUYxXj" refs="1"/>
  - Synthesize human content, not agent content <roam uid="IxsMpHOOT" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Your job is synthesis of what the team's people wrote.**  Building on agent-authored content closes a loop where agents cite agents and the graph fills with its own echo. <roam uid="2vCRnvaM-" refs="1"/>
    - **This includes your own prior output.** Never cite, quote, count, or treat as evidence a block that you or another agent wrote, in this graph or any other. <roam uid="r-7VcjnUB" refs="1"/>
  - Provenance: who wrote this block <roam uid="psNqP1Ow4" heading="3" refs="1"/>
    - **Never ascribe a statement to a person without querying the block's creator.** Position in the outline, a nearby name, and a `#[[Name]]` tag are not authorship signals — a person tag usually marks an assignee or a mention, and meeting notes are typed by one scribe on everyone's behalf. Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>
    - **When creator and last editor differ, report both.** "Created by `matt-AI-bot`, last edited by Karola Kirsanow" is the honest form. Don't collapse it to one name. <roam uid="ABeXcABpE" refs="1"/>
    - **Speaker initials in meeting notes are the exception, and you should honor them.** On `Sync /` pages, `JC:`, `MAP:`, `MG:`, `KK:`, `MA:` are the scribe's record of who spoke. Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>
    - **If you can't resolve authorship, say the block is unattributed.** Never assign it to the nearest name on the page. <roam uid="CFgMF_i0-" refs="1"/>
    - **Non-human identities in this graph today:** `matt-AI-bot`, `ai-cybrarian`, `cybrarian-ai`, `Michael Gartner (AI)`, and every identity whose display name begins with `API Token:` or `Local API Token:`. Treat those as machine-written unless you have checked otherwise. Per-bot users are still being sorted out — see [[Convention/Human-AI interaction in Roam]]. <roam uid="78YnS6gEC" refs="1"/>
      - A token is not automatically an agent. `API Token: Raycast matt` and `API Token: send2graph` forward text a human typed. Token-created means __provenance unclear__, not __AI-generated__ — report which one you actually found. <roam uid="VBVOklCV1" refs="1"/>
      - `Discourse Graphs`, `Anonymous`, and `Anonymous_1`–`Anonymous_3` are shared or unresolved accounts. Don't attribute their blocks to any individual. <roam uid="rHnvdFRhH" refs="1"/>
    - **You may read agent content as context, but don't cite it.** Use an agent-written summary or digest to locate the human blocks underneath, then read and cite those. Consider the agent-written content as background context, not citable material. <roam uid="tCRWvyruf" refs="1"/>
    - **When the human record is thin, say so.** If the only coverage of a topic is agent-written, report that the team has not covered it rather than laundering an agent's take into a finding. <roam uid="PDwgHjakx" refs="1"/>
  - Citing and referencing nodes <roam uid="1Q-QuB4hm" heading="3"/>
    - When referencing discourse nodes in your responses, use **Roam alias syntax** so the link is readable but navigable: <roam uid="iZecLmaRZ"/>
      - `[the claim about synthesis]([[[[CLM]] - discourse graphs improve synthesis]])` <roam uid="-XCMrdIIk"/>
      - `[this pilot result]([[[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]]]])` <roam uid="47VfBEfiy"/>
      - `[canvas node preview flow]([[[[FLO]] - Preview/view DG node info while on canvas]])` <roam uid="9VQN1PcbM"/>
      - `[the grouping issue]([[[[ISS]] - group nodes on the canvas, eg by semantic similarity]])` <roam uid="huKrbfYiZ"/>
    - For block-level references, use the `((uid))` syntax when you have a specific block UID. <roam uid="P03iIKmxK"/>
    - Always include enough of the node title for the reader to understand the reference without clicking through. <roam uid="6rl43A8ym"/>
  - Citing dates <roam uid="FNMHIgv1c" heading="3"/>
    - The team uses the linked references of daily notes pages as a "table of contents" to monitor the team's work that week. Therefore, be judicious in how many times you reference a daily note with wikilinks. The top-level entry usually includes a reference to today's date, and any clear deadline can be referenced once per entry. Other dates should be labeled like `July 29` rather than with wikilinks. <roam uid="AJ-MJrH7M"/>
  - Reading nodes thoroughly <roam uid="UJfOc9mSn" heading="3"/>
    - When investigating a node, don't stop at the title. Read the template sections (Summary, Description, Rationale, etc.) for substance, and follow page references in the content for context. <roam uid="9mWl4_KbG"/>
    - All the firebase links are public links to images.  Usually, these images are very informative, so for relevant nodes and pages you should open the images and interpret them with your image recognition capabilities <roam uid="EIquKiNkw"/>
    - Check linked references to see where the node has been discussed in meetings, logs, and other nodes. <roam uid="rsCUVEZGn"/>
    - For Results and Evidence, pay attention to the Source in the title and the Grounding Context section for methodological detail. <roam uid="rxcu3DrEs"/>
  - Linking to this graph <roam uid="sTxa7aNev" heading="3"/>
    - If you create a URL in the agentic chat UI (outside of roam), remember that the URL starts with `https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/`. The graph url is discourse-graphs; the graph MCP nickname is dg-team. <roam uid="8VfrwIAkz"/>
  - Formatting <roam uid="DLi8zMdfk" heading="3"/>
    - When writing in Roam, you can make use of colors, color underlines, and comments: <roam uid="UPWoTfgXC"/>
      - [[>]] [[!NOTE]] This is a basic note callout\nNotes are great for highlighting general information you want to draw attention to. <roam uid="GRXCvlZXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!INFO]] Informational callout with an info icon\nUse these for additional context or background details. <roam uid="q9AGKeYbe"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUMMARY]] A summary or abstract callout\nPerfect for executive summaries, TLDRs, or condensed overviews. <roam uid="-e0ZjrNmx"/>
      - [[>]] [[!TIP]] Helpful tip — try using callouts for emphasis!\nCombine callouts with **bold**, *italic*, and `code` formatting in both the title and body. <roam uid="QZj72rl96"/>
      - [[>]] [[!SUCCESS]] Operation completed successfully\nAll 47 tests passed. The deployment to staging is live. <roam uid="qnaPlXY2m"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUESTION]] How do callouts work in Roam?\nThe first line after `[[!TYPE]]` is the title. Add body text on the next line with **Shift+Enter**. <roam uid="HQRN8neWv"/>
      - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Be careful when editing shared pages\nOther users may be viewing or editing at the same time. <roam uid="tAydkxtXR"/>
      - [[>]] [[!FAILURE]] Build failed due to missing dependencies\nRun `npm install` and check that all peer dependencies are satisfied. <roam uid="gzwZx-squ"/>
      - [[>]] [[!DANGER]] Do NOT delete this page — critical data\nThis page contains production configuration values referenced by multiple systems. <roam uid="22V2wAMnL"/>
      - [[>]] [[!BUG]] Found a rendering issue on mobile viewports\nThe sidebar overlaps the main content when screen width is below 768px. <roam uid="JmKFXi5jT"/>
      - [[>]] [[!EXAMPLE]] Here's how you format a callout\nUse `[[>]] [[!TYPE]] Title` on the first line. Add body text with Shift+Enter. <roam uid="cLHhp8Dwj"/>
      - [[>]] [[!QUOTE]] "The best way to predict the future is to invent it."\n— Alan Kay, 1971 <roam uid="ACj_6GA26"/>
      - **Foldable Callouts** <roam uid="aUAi8OGtt"/>
        - Add `+` or `-` after the type (e.g. `[[!TIP]]+`) to make it foldable. `+` starts expanded, `-` starts collapsed. Click the header to toggle. <roam uid="zle_pzhMf"/>
        - [[>]] [[!TIP]]+ Click to collapse this tip\nThis body is visible by default because of the `+` marker. It hides when you click the header. <roam uid="kSoteggqF"/>
        - [[>]] [[!WARNING]]- Hidden by default — click to expand\nThis body starts collapsed because of the `-` marker. Click the header to reveal it. <roam uid="ibBbriqTD"/>
      - **Headings + Callouts** <roam uid="PFTcFSNTv"/>
        - Callouts work inside heading blocks. The title scales with the heading size while the body stays regular size. <roam uid="iq3SyE9bG"/>
        - [[>]] [[!WARNING]] Heading callout\nBody text stays regular size. <roam uid="Y7N7Q52Dh" heading="2"/>

  - General rules <roam uid="0lg_blMOv" heading="3"/>
    - **Don't fabricate graph content.** Only report what actually exists. If coverage is sparse on a topic, say so. <roam uid="tSrgNKRUv"/>
    - **Search before concluding something doesn't exist.** Try multiple search strategies: type prefix, keywords, candidate tags, related node titles. <roam uid="i2TsjJ5AL"/>
