content.content:
1	# Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="17"/>
2	
3	- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Working document: options and their costs, not decisions <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
4	  - This page maps the options for adding personal accounts to Discourse Graphs, so the group can choose. Only the items under "Constraints so far" are settled. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
5	  - This was written with OpenSpec, but because there are many pending decisions, we decided to stay at a pre-spec level. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
6	- Glossary <roam uid="8wg9mn-Kt"/>
7	  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs. <roam uid="V3WnEIow4"/>
8	  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, `everyone`, or an agent. <roam uid="pvL47ThL3"/>
9	  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person. <roam uid="aCzLIN3E9"/>
10	  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet. <roam uid="gav2kohTZ" refs="1"/>
11	  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault. <roam uid="QH3QWTy6q"/>
12	  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space. <roam uid="u7kJsZCjS"/>
13	  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. <roam uid="PrKq7VlbT"/>
14	  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`). <roam uid="_ditzi8bq"/>
15	  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who. <roam uid="w9yVmbPyd"/>
16	  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ"/>
17	    - `asserted`: only vouched for by a space session. Any co-member could have made it. <roam uid="tyAhKq0Iy"/>
18	    - `corroborated`: two or more spaces recorded the same platform account details before the claim (layer L2). <roam uid="F5NMd6BX2"/>
19	    - `attested`: proven by a check that a co-member can't fake, such as email binding (L1), a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8). <roam uid="LT9VSLIoK"/>
20	    - `frozen`: a competing claim arrived, and the claim gives no access until it is settled (L3). <roam uid="jssPobCiC"/>
21	  - **Access claim, identity claim**: an access claim only lets the person act in the vouching space. An identity claim says who the person is everywhere, and so carries attribution. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record. <roam uid="xwIIr5Cdw"/>
22	  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims. <roam uid="_blIoPRFG"/>
23	  - **Lease**: a person's access through a space lasts while they keep using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). 90 days is a placeholder. <roam uid="gegO9HCwc"/>
24	  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only. <roam uid="gIBK30HQq"/>
25	  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user. <roam uid="cqn2EyIWs"/>
26	  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not. <roam uid="u2sj1P4VN"/>
27	  - **Agent**: a pseudo-user for an AI agent. It reads what its one principal (a person or a space) reads, usually capped to read-only. <roam uid="Z4tFuDPOk"/>
28	- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
29	  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
30	  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
31	  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
32	  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
33	  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
34	  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
35	- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
36	  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
37	  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
38	  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
39	  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
40	    - Note from Michael: Actually we should look into the pros and cons of that assumption. Forcing accounts is harder on user, but there are engagement benefits. <roam uid="2YMqhsRfX"/>
41	  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
42	  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
43	  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
44	  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
45	  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>
46	- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
47	  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT"/>
48	    - One pseudo-user per space, with a shared space password stored in the platform settings. Every graph member can read that password. <roam uid="kb_Gd_svI"/>
49	    - One pseudo-user per group. <roam uid="IH0tyDi5Z"/>
50	    - The `everyone` pseudo-user for public content (ENG-1837 branch, not merged). <roam uid="oJCpZSrsO"/>
51	    - Agent users for read-only agent access (planned in the `agent-read-only-access` OpenSpec change). <roam uid="viJKLrjcB"/>
52	  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS"/>
53	    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
54	    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
55	  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
56	  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
57	    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
58	  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
59	- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
60	  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
61	  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
62	  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
63	  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
64	  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
65	  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
66	  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
67	  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
68	  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
69	  - ---- below this line, for later ----- <roam uid="IP1CB4pWB"/>
70	- Decision: how a [personal account](((gav2kohTZ))) is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
71	  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
72	  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
73	    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
74	    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
75	    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
76	    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
77	  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
78	    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
79	    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
80	    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
81	  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
82	    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
83	    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
84	    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
85	    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
86	  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
87	    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
88	    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
89	    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
90	  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
91	    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
92	    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
93	    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
94	      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
95	      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
96	    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
97	      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
98	      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
99	      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
100	      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
101	      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
102	        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
103	        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
104	        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
105	        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
106	    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
107	      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
108	      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
109	    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
110	      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
111	      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
112	      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
113	        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
114	        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
115	        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
116	        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
117	        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
118	    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
119	      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
120	      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
121	      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
122	      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
123	    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
124	      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
125	      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
126	    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
127	      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
128	      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
129	      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
130	      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
131	      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
132	        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
133	        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
134	        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
135	    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
136	      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
137	      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
138	    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
139	      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
140	      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
141	      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
142	      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
143	      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
144	        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
145	        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
146	        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
147	        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
148	      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
149	  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
150	    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>

# Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="17"/>

- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Working document: options and their costs, not decisions <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
  - This page maps the options for adding personal accounts to Discourse Graphs, so the group can choose. Only the items under "Constraints so far" are settled. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
  - This was written with OpenSpec, but because there are many pending decisions, we decided to stay at a pre-spec level. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Glossary <roam uid="8wg9mn-Kt"/>
  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs. <roam uid="V3WnEIow4"/>
  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, `everyone`, or an agent. <roam uid="pvL47ThL3"/>
  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person. <roam uid="aCzLIN3E9"/>
  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet. <roam uid="gav2kohTZ" refs="1"/>
  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault. <roam uid="QH3QWTy6q"/>
  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space. <roam uid="u7kJsZCjS"/>
  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. <roam uid="PrKq7VlbT"/>
  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`). <roam uid="_ditzi8bq"/>
  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who. <roam uid="w9yVmbPyd"/>
  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ"/>
    - `asserted`: only vouched for by a space session. Any co-member could have made it. <roam uid="tyAhKq0Iy"/>
    - `corroborated`: two or more spaces recorded the same platform account details before the claim (layer L2). <roam uid="F5NMd6BX2"/>
    - `attested`: proven by a check that a co-member can't fake, such as email binding (L1), a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8). <roam uid="LT9VSLIoK"/>
    - `frozen`: a competing claim arrived, and the claim gives no access until it is settled (L3). <roam uid="jssPobCiC"/>
  - **Access claim, identity claim**: an access claim only lets the person act in the vouching space. An identity claim says who the person is everywhere, and so carries attribution. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record. <roam uid="xwIIr5Cdw"/>
  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims. <roam uid="_blIoPRFG"/>
  - **Lease**: a person's access through a space lasts while they keep using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). 90 days is a placeholder. <roam uid="gegO9HCwc"/>
  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only. <roam uid="gIBK30HQq"/>
  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user. <roam uid="cqn2EyIWs"/>
  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not. <roam uid="u2sj1P4VN"/>
  - **Agent**: a pseudo-user for an AI agent. It reads what its one principal (a person or a space) reads, usually capped to read-only. <roam uid="Z4tFuDPOk"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
    - Note from Michael: Actually we should look into the pros and cons of that assumption. Forcing accounts is harder on user, but there are engagement benefits. <roam uid="2YMqhsRfX"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>
- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT"/>
    - One pseudo-user per space, with a shared space password stored in the platform settings. Every graph member can read that password. <roam uid="kb_Gd_svI"/>
    - One pseudo-user per group. <roam uid="IH0tyDi5Z"/>
    - The `everyone` pseudo-user for public content (ENG-1837 branch, not merged). <roam uid="oJCpZSrsO"/>
    - Agent users for read-only agent access (planned in the `agent-read-only-access` OpenSpec change). <roam uid="viJKLrjcB"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` already references `auth.users`. Today only the space pseudo-account sets it. <roam uid="f6tgGk3-t"/>
    - `upsert_account_in_space` already writes a `SpaceAccess` row for an account whose `dg_account` is set. This anticipates personal accounts with copied grants. <roam uid="umtrUcTmK"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK"/>
    - ENG-1837 adds `everyone` to it. The agent change adds the agent's principal and that principal's groups. Personal accounts would be the third change to this function. <roam uid="bUiWiBwvl"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`. An Obsidian account looks local to its vault (not verified). <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agent grants owned by a person: an agent reads what its person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
  - ---- below this line, for later ----- <roam uid="IP1CB4pWB"/>
- Decision: how a [personal account](((gav2kohTZ))) is linked to a platform identity <roam uid="HrW3SuczV"/>
  - **Why it matters:** anyone who holds a space password can claim to be any member of that space. This decision sets how much proof a link needs, and therefore whether a co-member can take over another member's attribution and their access to other spaces. Stronger proof costs the person effort or depends on Roam. <roam uid="G_ksAI6Q_"/>
  - The threat <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl"/>
    - Anyone with the space password can mint a claim as that space. In Roam, that is every graph member. <roam uid="3TQldEoEj"/>
    - A co-member can therefore claim another member's Roam uid and take over their attribution, and their access to other spaces if the claim spreads beyond the space. <roam uid="8miESmtZh"/>
    - Outsiders can't do this under any option below. <roam uid="EJZYtvlMR"/>
    - Example: Mallory reads graph A's space password, calls `create_secret_token` as the space with Alice's uid in the payload, opens the link, and logs in with her own Google account. `create_secret_token` accepts any payload from any authenticated caller. <roam uid="6gK3VqcE-"/>
  - Two kinds of claim <roam uid="_oWUtNrtr"/>
    - An access claim is an `asserted` claim: "I am this platform account", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have. <roam uid="qbzJP8qlz"/>
    - An identity claim says "this platform account is me". It carries attribution and may spread to other spaces, so it needs stronger proof. <roam uid="jriBBo825"/>
    - The group wants identity, not only access. <roam uid="tre8QheiL"/>
  - Verified identifiers are separate from links <roam uid="o_xM2FmbI"/>
    - A personal account can hold verified identifiers that aren't tied to any platform account: emails, Google or GitHub identities, an ORCID iD, an ATProto handle. <roam uid="rvWITqil4"/>
    - They serve login, the profile, and attribution on their own. <roam uid="cMWL7UAPb"/>
    - An identifier becomes evidence for a link only when a platform records the same identifier for a platform account. That is what L1 checks for email. <roam uid="Q1mfw83z-"/>
    - Obsidian attribution relies on these identifiers, since Obsidian rarely records anything we can check. <roam uid="dPJOYzQfI"/>
  - Email as the bridge <roam uid="WbpaSzu1V"/>
    - The Roam plugin can read `:user/email` through datalog. <roam uid="q37Xq8DVO"/>
    - If the personal account proves control of an email (Google login, or a verification mail) and Roam records that email for the uid, a forger fails: they can't log in as the victim's email. <roam uid="Zt5yx9RoU"/>
    - The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. If it comes from the claim's own payload, the forger writes their own email. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts. <roam uid="Qr1nAWi-I"/>
  - Layers <roam uid="tZGbhisXM"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the layers are the choices for the identity-link decision. Each one stops a different kind of forgery, at a different cost to the person and to us. The packages below combine them, so read those first if you only want the trade-offs. <roam uid="jY7-WynXq"/>
    - The layers stack. Each one is described by what it stops and what it costs. <roam uid="fBoQ0vuf5"/>
    - L0: Token handoff only. The plugin mints a `secret_token` with the uid; the person logs in on the Website. <roam uid="_qMYaUHJ0"/>
      - Stops outsiders only. <roam uid="ZjIn7a1og"/>
      - Burden: none. Cost: lowest, reuses the `auth/token` route. Platforms: all. <roam uid="bM5E9fXbZ"/>
    - L1: Email binding. The personal account must control the email that the platform records for the platform account. <roam uid="ShFzQ-cQE"/>
      - Control of the email can be proven two ways, both at this layer: a verification mail, or a linked external identity (Google, GitHub, ...) whose provider vouches that the email is verified. Many Roam users sign in to Roam with Google, so the same Google account often proves the match in one step. <roam uid="0ngOboLPC"/>
      - Only provider emails marked as verified count. Supabase also links identities that share a verified email automatically, so the account's set of verified emails must be read from the account, not from one login. <roam uid="L3hwsR2X1"/>
      - Stops a forger who can't also falsify the binding source. <roam uid="eNir7ER3F"/>
      - Burden: the person verifies once. Cost: low. The verification can start from any plugin or from the Website. Platforms: any platform that records an email for the account. Roam does; for Obsidian, see below. <roam uid="KgXX_YwXm"/>
      - Obsidian <roam uid="cx9aeX2_F"/>
        - The Obsidian plugin sends no email today (`email: undefined` in `supabaseContext.ts`). Whether it can read the email of the Obsidian account, and whether that email is verified, is not checked yet. Using an Obsidian account is optional, so some users have none. <roam uid="sx3sITsvn"/>
        - The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there. <roam uid="AM08ShSzs"/>
        - An email the person types in is not a platform record. Verifying it gives the personal account a verified identifier, but says nothing about which platform account is theirs. <roam uid="nvfy6pgBo"/>
        - A vault synced between people shares one `PlatformAccount`, so a claim by one of them covers the others' content too. <roam uid="vBcLpeOcv"/>
    - L2: Corroboration. Accept the binding only if two or more spaces recorded it before the claim. <roam uid="sZ85qtOYg"/>
      - Stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs. <roam uid="SK6ZmyFfB"/>
      - Burden: none, but people in a single graph never reach this level. Cost: low, a query over existing rows. <roam uid="-I0HJIpta"/>
    - L3: Conflict detection and notification. Freeze a uid when a competing claim arrives; mail the verified address when a link is made. <roam uid="IjOxjCi1x"/>
      - Prevents nothing, but a forgery is noticed fast and can be reversed. <roam uid="QBboyIbUv"/>
      - Burden: the victim reacts to a notice; someone settles frozen links. Cost: low to medium. Platforms: all. <roam uid="R0WJRywXw"/>
      - Variant: the victim's plugin checks on load <roam uid="_lAmRuC9k"/>
        - The plugin knows the current Roam uid from its own client. On load it asks whether that `PlatformAccount` is claimed. If it is claimed and the person has no personal session, or a different one, the plugin asks "Your Roam identity is linked to a Discourse Graphs account. Was this you?" <roam uid="FNfpjab1n"/>
        - Catches a forgery without email, even when the forger controls the email binding. The damage window lasts until the victim next opens the plugin. <roam uid="ovhYlp3bV"/>
        - Needs a new `SECURITY DEFINER` function that returns only the claim status, not the claimant. `my_accounts` no longer exposes `dg_account`. <roam uid="HU4VT8div"/>
        - Under the space session the caller only asserts their uid, so any member can ask about any co-member ("has X connected a Discourse Graphs account?"). With L8, the plugin can present the Firebase token and the function answers only for the proven uid. <roam uid="NxNh0_jLj"/>
        - Responding can't rest on a bare assertion: if anyone could freeze a claim, a forger could freeze every legitimate claim in the graph. A contest must either bring a proof stronger than the existing claim's attestation (L1, L8), or only notify and flag for review. <roam uid="03ZvE1H1-"/>
    - L4: Per-device keys, trusted on first use. The plugin silently registers a key per browser and Roam user; identity claims must be signed by a registered key. <roam uid="OlDRHI2bI"/>
      - Stops forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run. A key added later for the same uid shows up on the older device as "a new device was registered as you". <roam uid="oZz6BVWjI"/>
      - Burden: users confirm new devices. Cost: medium. Platforms: Roam and Obsidian. <roam uid="_Dcxp_ILa"/>
      - Works without a personal account, so it protects people who never sign up. <roam uid="qKkvxmlvM"/>
      - Caveat: in Roam, every extension shares the roamresearch.com origin. Another extension can use the key while the page is open, but can't export it. <roam uid="HNbfUd67I"/>
    - L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xp07QYFwB"/>
      - Stops forgery by anyone except the admin. <roam uid="H5d_3BrMU"/>
      - Burden: admins, once per claim. Cost: medium, needs the admin role first. Only as strong as the admin proof. <roam uid="hlhlB4Hzw"/>
    - L6: Roam backend attestation. Our server reads the uid-to-email binding from Roam with a graph token. <roam uid="xZ9ZW0mBc"/>
      - Stops all forgery. <roam uid="XbTu0uESn"/>
      - Needs an active Roam subscription to create a backend token. L6 can therefore only be an optional upgrade, never a requirement. <roam uid="aUGQqVVU0"/>
      - A Roam uid is global, so a one-time token from any graph the person owns is enough. No shared-graph admin is needed. <roam uid="-ubL7d6ZM"/>
      - Burden: the person supplies a token once (or an admin stores one). Cost: medium one-time, high if stored (secrets, rotation). Platforms: Roam only. <roam uid="csHZObWSP"/>
      - Variant: a token stored per graph, supplied by an admin. <roam uid="j0wLV46uO"/>
        - Our server can then attest the uid-to-email binding of any member of that graph. Members don't need their own Roam subscription, so L6 becomes available to everyone in that graph. <roam uid="xyNjRWm5g"/>
        - The same token can first attest the admin who supplies it, so their proven admin flag lands on the right `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="IskrgBXJ4"/>
        - Cost: a read-only graph token exposes the whole graph, which is far more than Discourse Graphs stores. It needs encrypted storage readable only by a server-side function (for example Supabase Vault), never by clients. The admin can revoke it in Roam at any time, and then the graph falls back to the weaker layers. <roam uid="WxoAJVdJR"/>
    - L7: Tiered space password. Members get a reader credential; admins hold the editor credential. <roam uid="ipLQprIac"/>
      - Stops forgery by non-admins. <roam uid="TD5X_nVgo"/>
      - Burden: admins distribute and rotate credentials. Cost: medium, and it changes who can sync. <roam uid="dE_FI2cS_"/>
    - L8: Roam sign-in token (candidate). The plugin reads the signed-in user's Firebase ID token from the page and sends it to our server, which checks it and discards it. <roam uid="J0BDirkni"/>
      - Roam uses Firebase Auth. Its ID token is a JWT signed by Google, with issuer `https://securetoken.google.com/firescript-577a2`. Its claims include the Roam uid (`sub`), the user's email, and `email_verified` (true in the test). The token expires after about an hour. Checked in the Roam desktop app on 2026-10-24. <roam uid="6BQcIhrfL"/>
      - Our server can check the signature against Google's public keys and the audience `firescript-577a2`, without any Roam token. A co-member can't produce another user's token without running code in that user's browser. <roam uid="V1kVD6tTP"/>
      - Stops all forgery, like L6, and works for every Roam user, with no subscription and no admin. <roam uid="zLeqJYcuA"/>
      - Burden: none for the person. Cost: low to medium, one server-side check. <roam uid="QJauyMm3T"/>
      - Caveats <roam uid="Mg5o9FT2O"/>
        - **Blocking: L8 can't be used until we have checked that it doesn't violate Roam's Terms of Service, and Roam has agreed.** Reading another product's session token and sending it to our server may breach those terms even if we only verify it and discard it. <roam uid="on38t4VGv"/>
        - It depends on Roam's internals: the token sits in IndexedDB (`firebaseLocalStorageDb`), which Roam can change without notice. <roam uid="e0BzqzHvE"/>
        - The token also authenticates to Roam itself for about an hour. Our server would briefly hold a credential that can act as the user in Roam. <roam uid="k0stwVkUB"/>
        - Only the short-lived ID token may leave the browser, never the refresh token. <roam uid="Q_jKLTAGF"/>
      - Also checked in a browser on 2026-10-24, in a normal and a private window: the same storage holds the same kind of token. The browser has one auth entry where the desktop app has two (the app adds a `-tx-writer` entry), so the plugin should read the `[DEFAULT]` entry. <roam uid="tRm3RsaGT"/>
  - Packages to compare <roam uid="N3CzNT6ji"/>
    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>

content.text: Read the first 150 of 428 lines of the spec page; reading the rest now before drafting the ladder.

content.content:
150	    - Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
151	    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
152	    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
153	    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
154	    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
155	    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
156	  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
157	    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
158	    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
159	    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
160	    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
161	- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
162	  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
163	  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
164	    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
165	    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
166	      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
167	      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
168	  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
169	    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
170	    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
171	    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
172	  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
173	    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
174	      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
175	      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>
176	      - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FWtj7oz4ioH.svg?alt=media&token=4eed2225-0f3a-432b-aa4f-f61301450a10) <roam uid="5JgqmEZzH"/>
177	    - Option 2: reach scoped by attestation. Preferred so far. <roam uid="bpN-mO9lF"/>
178	      - The claim record holds the person, the `PlatformAccount`, the vouching space (the space whose session made the claim), and the attestation level. <roam uid="2GK3rGpKk"/>
179	      - An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space. <roam uid="28rjLezNq"/>
180	      - A `corroborated` or `attested` claim gives access in every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="qmd_UoR4o"/>
181	      - A forged assertion stays in a space whose password the forger already holds, so it gains nothing. <roam uid="mSMyEGsZg"/>
182	      - Proving identity later widens the reach in place, with no new kind of record. <roam uid="yb6-e7E5i"/>
183	      - Cost: with weakly proven claims, the person connects each space once. <roam uid="YiPQJDhje"/>
184	      - Cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="9M61pEmt1"/>
185	      - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FMPJR41V-g1.svg?alt=media&token=fd95e907-4990-47ef-8183-e406c0352c6b) <roam uid="t5rQPGNQ3"/>
186	  - Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
187	    - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
188	    - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
189	    - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. The agent access design notes the same cost. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
190	    - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
191	    - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
192	    - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
193	    - Agent grants: the same pattern inside `my_user_accounts()` as `agent_grant`, but a different table. An agent has exactly one principal and is gated by its role claim. An agent owned by a person adds one level: agent, person, space, group. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>
194	  - Prerequisite <roam uid="huOP3R6up"/>
195	    - The `group_membership` insert hole is closed first (see Constraints). It lets any caller join a uid that has no members, and space pseudo-users have none, so it already exposes spaces today (found by reading the policy, not tested). <roam uid="EogAwWnXT"/>
196	- Decision: whether to hide user ids from other clients <roam uid="s86_P-XTI" refs="1"/>
197	  - **Why it matters:** with personal accounts, `auth.users.id` will identify people, not only spaces and groups. This decision sets whether we keep those ids away from other clients, or make sure that knowing one gives no power. Leaning: make a known id harmless, and don't try to hide it everywhere. <roam uid="UE2PEVfE3"/>
198	  - Where other clients can read a user id today <roam uid="Z_RS5cbwK"/>
199	    - `SpaceAccess.account_uid` and `ResourceAccess.account_uid`: anyone with `reader` access to the space. These hold space login accounts and groups. <roam uid="ncHhD0VTQ"/>
200	    - `group_membership.member_id`: other members of the group. <roam uid="h__0XthP6"/>
201	    - `my_pseudo_accounts.dg_account`: other members of the group. It lists space login accounts only. <roam uid="hl4MhKDJ9"/>
202	    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` and `my_accounts.dg_account`: anyone with `partial` access to a space that uses the account. Production had no such row with a value on November 4, 2026, but claims will add them. <roam uid="EIngeKqbQ"/>
203	  - Option A: treat a user id as an identifier, and make sure it proves nothing <roam uid="QcS_o6QFx"/>
204	    - A known id gives no power over its user. ENG-2438 stops a user from joining another user's access. ENG-2456 stops direct adds to a group, and limits space and resource grants to the caller and the caller's groups. <roam uid="MLIbACl4p"/>
205	    - A user id doesn't show which platform accounts belong to one person. ENG-2441 hides `dg_account` from clients, through the `my_accounts` view and through a column grant on `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="kxrCwBvhv"/>
206	    - New checks must follow one rule: a user id is an identifier, never proof of anything. <roam uid="imG_IERsN"/>
207	    - Cost: a person's user id stays visible to the other members of their groups. Without `dg_account`, it doesn't lead to their platform accounts. <roam uid="X1QHARHDW"/>
208	    - Limit: `AgentIdentifier.value` is readable from `reader` access. Where it holds an email, it can still link one person's accounts across spaces. <roam uid="GEafzgFaU"/>
209	  - Option B: option A, and also hide user ids from clients that don't strictly need them <roam uid="0sknqBAbn"/>
210	    - Narrow `SpaceAccess`, `ResourceAccess` and `group_membership` to the caller's own rows, with group admins still seeing their group's members. <roam uid="mougM6VrB"/>
211	    - Replace `dg_account` in `my_pseudo_accounts` with another handle. Add definer functions for removing a member and setting an admin. <roam uid="ZkvVcLzTe"/>
212	    - For: <roam uid="rLizJTRoC"/>
213	      - It adds a second layer if a future check wrongly trusts a user id. <roam uid="5-oj46v9h"/>
214	      - Fewer clients see people's ids once people join groups directly. <roam uid="VCK0A32IZ"/>
215	      - Readers of a space don't see who else has access. <roam uid="APgD7Hjar"/>
216	    - Against: <roam uid="i0NOyj1RW"/>
217	      - It doesn't replace option A. Ids that were already read stay known, so a known id must be harmless anyway. <roam uid="x7plujA4H"/>
218	      - It can't be complete. Group members need group ids, and group admins need a way to name members. <roam uid="GICJgztPZ"/>
219	      - `group_membership` can't use column grants, because shipped plugins filter on `member_id`. <roam uid="T8sJ4q1QP"/>
220	      - Changing `my_pseudo_accounts` conflicts with ENG-2444, which keeps every view's columns. <roam uid="bT8yfDiON"/>
221	      - Each new table with a user id needs the same care. <roam uid="JPrKyLLVj"/>
222	      - Estimated cost: 3 to 4 days on top of option A. <roam uid="qasR_Z5EG"/>
223	  - Revisit option B if a feature needs a person's user id to stay private from people who share a space or a group with them. <roam uid="3_Cr4tT4b"/>
224	- Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5" refs="1"/>
225	  - **Why it matters:** every access policy calls these functions, so they set what each caller reaches and add to the cost of every query. Most of this section is agreed; only the lease length is open. <roam uid="mcAP4xcAU"/>
226	  - Where the claim lives, without a new table <roam uid="Cq8Z7k1_K"/>
227	    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account`: the person who claimed the account (exists today). <roam uid="HI27RxILB"/>
228	    - `PlatformAccount.claim_attestation`: asserted, corroborated, attested, or frozen. <roam uid="LpZMlh92m"/>
229	    - `LocalAccess.vouched`: this space's session made the claim. <roam uid="Aw4Af4gJG"/>
230	    - `LocalAccess.last_seen`: the lease. <roam uid="vZYlXEL7h"/>
231	    - `LocalAccess` admin level and delegated flag: the space-admin decision. <roam uid="p3wczF1ke"/>
232	    - Each space's pseudo-user uid is needed. Today it is found through the anonymous `PlatformAccount`, whose `account_local_id` is `get_space_anonymous_email(platform, id)`. A `Space.principal_uid` column would be clearer. <roam uid="IRNBzF_Oa"/>
233	  - Permissions stay in `SpaceAccess`; `LocalAccess` records use and the claim <roam uid="36Yd-0vay"/>
234	    - `LocalAccess` means a platform account is used in a space. With claims, it also records how strong the claim is (`vouched`, `last_seen`, attestation). <roam uid="_xHiqK5FF"/>
235	    - Permissions in a space come only from `SpaceAccess`. Claim strength in `LocalAccess` can cap them, but never grant them. <roam uid="vTZOkHOgl"/>
236	    - Today `LocalAccess` gives the account nothing in the space. It gives the space's members rights over the account: members can read it, and editors can edit or delete it while it is unowned. <roam uid="GyNZ1qUAM"/>
237	    - Editors need to insert and update those accounts, because they create the platform accounts of authors who may never log in. They don't need to delete them, and dropping delete also removes the cascade through `Document.author_id`. Claiming an account should not be one of those rights: see ((vtxvgZEKp))<ref>Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account</ref>. <roam uid="LhDhvYx-k"/>
238	  - Open: keeping the claim (`dg_account`) out of ordinary account writes <roam uid="vdV1jigrm" refs="3"/>
239	    - **Why it matters:** editors must keep writing the platform accounts of their space's authors, but claiming is a separate operation with its own rules. Today any editor of a space can claim its unowned accounts (((vtxvgZEKp))). Not decided; postponed. <roam uid="e3dHDdJ0k"/>
240	    - Option 1, column privileges: revoke `INSERT` and `UPDATE` on `PlatformAccount` from `authenticated`, then grant them back on every column except `dg_account`. A table-level grant covers all columns, so revoking the one column alone does not work. Cost: each new column has to be added to the grants, and a client upsert that sends `dg_account`, even as null, fails. <roam uid="XbS0B2zbY"/>
241	    - Option 2, a separate table for the claim: the link between a person and a platform account moves out of `PlatformAccount`, and only the claim path writes it. This departs from "Where the claim lives, without a new table" above. <roam uid="eXQzoqBsj"/>
242	    - Both options route claims through a `SECURITY DEFINER` claim function that holds the claim rules in one place. If the claim moves later, only the function body changes. The Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` is the only code that sets `dg_account` today, so it would call that function. <roam uid="ftEJrOez4"/>
243	    - Interim, October 30: `authenticated` can no longer write `dg_account` (column privileges, see ((vtxvgZEKp))<ref>Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account</ref>). Whatever claim mechanism this spec picks starts from there. <roam uid="JfuWa2pWN"/>
244	  - Three nested sets of uids for a caller <roam uid="mEKDhdnT_"/>
245	    - `self_to_spaces()`: the caller, plus the spaces the caller acts for through claims (reach rule, lease, not frozen). <roam uid="9DQlyb6HQ"/>
246	    - `self_to_groups()`: that, plus the groups of every uid in it. One pass over `group_membership`, no recursion. <roam uid="xgb-TmzcC"/>
247	    - `self_to_everyone()`: that, plus the `everyone` pseudo-user. Replaces `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="p_XEWf7L1"/>
248	    - These replace `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. Outside SQL, both names only appear in the generated `dbTypes.ts`. <roam uid="25IooWjth"/>
249	  - Which set each check uses <roam uid="bZ325OCEt"/>
250	    - Membership and admin checks on a group use `self_to_spaces()`. Groups don't count, otherwise membership would nest. `everyone` never counts. <roam uid="V3mJeIE0I"/>
251	    - Checks for sharing a space with an account use `self_to_groups()`. A public grant must not count as sharing. <roam uid="_xnlnN4_m"/>
252	    - Reads use `self_to_everyone()`. <roam uid="XOZ7nL4S6"/>
253	  - Each set is computed for one principal and works for any caller <roam uid="-7GZXBiOr"/>
254	    - Space session: the space and its groups, the same as today. <roam uid="INz7A6X98"/>
255	    - Person: the person, their direct groups, their claimed spaces, and those spaces' groups. <roam uid="9wwDV7p4T"/>
256	    - Agent: its own expansion, plus the full expansion of its principal from `agent_grant`. <roam uid="pul5mAdGy"/>
257	  - Group admin <roam uid="GNGlWJVoz"/>
258	    - Stage 1: `is_group_admin(G)` is true when any uid in `self_to_spaces()` is an admin of G. A person who acts for space S is an admin of G whenever S is. This lets people be promoted to direct group admins without being direct members first. <roam uid="gparhcgzS"/>
259	    - Stage 2: restrict the space-derived part to people who are admins of S. It waits until space admins exist. <roam uid="ziRKyT9d4"/>

261	    - `my_pseudo_accounts` must check `self_to_spaces()` instead of `auth.uid()`. Otherwise a person never sees the groups of their spaces, and publishing to groups finds none. <roam uid="F5fgLmqoL"/>
262	  - Agreed <roam uid="cCtIzCldr"/>
263	    - Caps: the sets return each uid with a cap, as `TABLE(uid, cap)` rather than bare uids. Permission checks use the lower of the grant and the cap. A group reached through a capped space inherits the cap. The same mechanism covers read-only access through a space and read-only agents. <roam uid="vLHTviSzs"/>
264	    - Cost: for a person, each call walks `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `Space` and `group_membership`. That is fine once per statement but not once per row, so the RLS rewrite to the `= ANY((SELECT ...))` pattern becomes a prerequisite. <roam uid="SyoGpN9DQ"/>
265	  - Open: the lease length (90 days is a placeholder). <roam uid="IN5YpaEA5"/>
266	  - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FoMbD_1Xs-h.svg?alt=media&token=ff8aabdb-be87-480d-932b-ead0847ffe4d) <roam uid="0mR6YMCry"/>
267	  - {{dg-canvas: [[Canvas/ DG account]]}} <roam uid="fHh1eG1Sn"/>
268	- Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>
269	  - Space admin <roam uid="3l40D2TI3"/>
270	    - **Why it matters:** every admin power is something any holder of the space password can do today, for example rotating that password or joining groups for the space. The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together. <roam uid="YyVfTf1I1"/>
271	    - Guessed: the plugin reports who is admin. <roam uid="RBdmXSvZj"/>
272	      - Roam: the plugin reads `roamAlphaAPI.user.isAdmin` ([developer documentation](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/U5DkRU6hr)). It is synchronous, takes no parameters, and answers only for the current user. This replaces the earlier guess, the first user page created in the graph. <roam uid="SdqDeXOxt"/>
273	        - The plugin can't ask about other users, so an admin is recorded only once that admin runs the plugin. Until then the space has no admin at this tier. <roam uid="xP-d6GZl_"/>
274	        - To check: the documentation says "an admin of this graph (the graph owner)". Roam graphs can have several admins besides the owner, so it is unclear whether the flag is true for the other admins or only for the owner. <roam uid="2MkuVao0B"/>
275	      - Obsidian: the only user. <roam uid="L_SdOpU7g"/>
276	      - Website: the creator of the space. <roam uid="Gbpn8W21T"/>
277	      - Forgeable on every platform: the plugin sends the report under the space session, so a co-member who holds the space password can report themselves as admin. L8 would prove which Roam user is calling, but not that this user is an admin. In Roam, L6 closes the gap for the admin who supplies a backend token: only admins can create one, and the same token lets our server attest which Roam user they are. That admin moves to the proven tier; other admins stay guessed. <roam uid="yhMBFbag9"/>
278	    - Registered: the person who first connected the space. Not recorded today. <roam uid="BLTnvtton"/>
