- Minimal: L0 + L1 + L3. Co-member forgery is detected after the fact. Almost no burden. <roam uid="3nc-Wa1fB"/>
    - Medium: Minimal + L2 + L4. Co-member forgery is prevented, except before the victim's first plugin use. Burden: new-device prompts. <roam uid="lpEuCPPEP"/>
    - Strong: Medium + L6 with a one-time token, for people who have a Roam subscription. Forgery is prevented for them. Burden: one token per person, once. Everyone else stays at Medium. <roam uid="ES2_RxYVo"/>
    - Admin-centric: L0 + L5 + L3. Set aside with L5. <roam uid="zo5JtOuJ8"/>
    - Because L6 is optional, Medium is the strongest level every user can reach. In it, L4 does most of the work against co-member forgery. <roam uid="GELnQvnLI"/>
    - Strong for everyone, if L8 is allowed: Medium + L8. Forgery is prevented for every Roam user, with no token and no subscription. Depends on Roam's agreement and on its internals staying stable. <roam uid="tsWkLqVnK"/>
  - Applies to every option <roam uid="inXsU_Qm3"/>
    - Record an attestation level on each link (`asserted`, `corroborated`, `attested`) and let policies read the level, never the platform. This lets us start low and add layers without migrating policies. <roam uid="UfKqf9ASZ"/>
    - Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links. <roam uid="w7SPEavvQ"/>
    - Platform-specific verification is expected. Multi-user platforms (Roam) have a server that can attest identity; local single-user platforms (Obsidian) have no co-member to forge against. <roam uid="mk9A0_wN6"/>
    - Obsidian links stay `asserted` in every option. Obsidian attribution comes from the person's verified identifiers, not from the platform account. <roam uid="eGU1Y7Vyj"/>
- Decision: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets which spaces a personal account can read and act for. The open question, how far a weakly proven claim reaches, decides whether cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="NQeAiZ8V4"/>
  - Ruled out <roam uid="1FYnwOB2T"/>
    - A: copy `SpaceAccess` and group rows to the person. The copies outlive the relation they came from. <roam uid="BGRs-LBmc"/>
    - Any edge from a person to a space that skips the `PlatformAccount`. This rules out B (the person as a member of the space pseudo-user in `group_membership`) and a separate person-to-space table. <roam uid="FKZQENpx6"/>
      - The `PlatformAccount` is where a person exists inside a space. Authorship, `LocalAccess` and identifiers hang off it. <roam uid="Z4r63tySQ"/>
      - A second track could disagree with it: a person could have a space's access through one edge while their `PlatformAccount` in that space is unclaimed, or claimed by someone else. <roam uid="2xyckcERL"/>
  - Model: claims through a PlatformAccount <roam uid="j2yrxCKys"/>
    - A claim links a personal account to a `PlatformAccount`. The person then acts for spaces where that `PlatformAccount` has a `LocalAccess` row. <roam uid="GMJo8AmA_"/>
    - `my_user_accounts()` adds those spaces' pseudo-users and the spaces' groups. The depth is fixed: one extra join, no recursion. <roam uid="5xZCf-gL6"/>
    - A person can also be a direct member of real groups, for example as a group admin. <roam uid="BobollM8N"/>
  - Open: how far a claim reaches <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm"/>
    - Option 1: reach follows identity. <roam uid="tYOGxPCv6"/>
      - Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="KS_8ViwDE"/>
      - Access needs identity proof first, so cross-space search waits on the identity-link decision. <roam uid="K210qCY9T"/>
      - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FWtj7oz4ioH.svg?alt=media&token=4eed2225-0f3a-432b-aa4f-f61301450a10) <roam uid="5JgqmEZzH"/>
    - Option 2: reach scoped by attestation. Preferred so far. <roam uid="bpN-mO9lF"/>
      - The claim record holds the person, the `PlatformAccount`, the vouching space (the space whose session made the claim), and the attestation level. <roam uid="2GK3rGpKk"/>
      - An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space. <roam uid="28rjLezNq"/>
      - A `corroborated` or `attested` claim gives access in every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="qmd_UoR4o"/>
      - A forged assertion stays in a space whose password the forger already holds, so it gains nothing. <roam uid="mSMyEGsZg"/>
      - Proving identity later widens the reach in place, with no new kind of record. <roam uid="yb6-e7E5i"/>
      - Cost: with weakly proven claims, the person connects each space once. <roam uid="YiPQJDhje"/>
      - Cross-space search can ship before the identity-link decision. <roam uid="9M61pEmt1"/>
      - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FMPJR41V-g1.svg?alt=media&token=fd95e907-4990-47ef-8183-e406c0352c6b) <roam uid="t5rQPGNQ3"/>
  - Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
    - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
    - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
    - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. The agent access design notes the same cost. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
    - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
    - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
    - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
    - Agent grants: the same pattern inside `my_user_accounts()` as `agent_grant`, but a different table. An agent has exactly one principal and is gated by its role claim. An agent owned by a person adds one level: agent, person, space, group. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>
  - Prerequisite <roam uid="huOP3R6up"/>
    - The `group_membership` insert hole is closed first (see Constraints). It lets any caller join a uid that has no members, and space pseudo-users have none, so it already exposes spaces today (found by reading the policy, not tested). <roam uid="EogAwWnXT"/>
- Decision: whether to hide user ids from other clients <roam uid="s86_P-XTI" refs="1"/>
  - **Why it matters:** with personal accounts, `auth.users.id` will identify people, not only spaces and groups. This decision sets whether we keep those ids away from other clients, or make sure that knowing one gives no power. Leaning: make a known id harmless, and don't try to hide it everywhere. <roam uid="UE2PEVfE3"/>
  - Where other clients can read a user id today <roam uid="Z_RS5cbwK"/>
    - `SpaceAccess.account_uid` and `ResourceAccess.account_uid`: anyone with `reader` access to the space. These hold space login accounts and groups. <roam uid="ncHhD0VTQ"/>
    - `group_membership.member_id`: other members of the group. <roam uid="h__0XthP6"/>
    - `my_pseudo_accounts.dg_account`: other members of the group. It lists space login accounts only. <roam uid="hl4MhKDJ9"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account` and `my_accounts.dg_account`: anyone with `partial` access to a space that uses the account. Production had no such row with a value on November 4, 2026, but claims will add them. <roam uid="EIngeKqbQ"/>
  - Option A: treat a user id as an identifier, and make sure it proves nothing <roam uid="QcS_o6QFx"/>
    - A known id gives no power over its user. ENG-2438 stops a user from joining another user's access. ENG-2456 stops direct adds to a group, and limits space and resource grants to the caller and the caller's groups. <roam uid="MLIbACl4p"/>
    - A user id doesn't show which platform accounts belong to one person. ENG-2441 hides `dg_account` from clients, through the `my_accounts` view and through a column grant on `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="kxrCwBvhv"/>
    - New checks must follow one rule: a user id is an identifier, never proof of anything. <roam uid="imG_IERsN"/>
    - Cost: a person's user id stays visible to the other members of their groups. Without `dg_account`, it doesn't lead to their platform accounts. <roam uid="X1QHARHDW"/>
    - Limit: `AgentIdentifier.value` is readable from `reader` access. Where it holds an email, it can still link one person's accounts across spaces. <roam uid="GEafzgFaU"/>
  - Option B: option A, and also hide user ids from clients that don't strictly need them <roam uid="0sknqBAbn"/>
    - Narrow `SpaceAccess`, `ResourceAccess` and `group_membership` to the caller's own rows, with group admins still seeing their group's members. <roam uid="mougM6VrB"/>
    - Replace `dg_account` in `my_pseudo_accounts` with another handle. Add definer functions for removing a member and setting an admin. <roam uid="ZkvVcLzTe"/>
    - For: <roam uid="rLizJTRoC"/>
      - It adds a second layer if a future check wrongly trusts a user id. <roam uid="5-oj46v9h"/>
      - Fewer clients see people's ids once people join groups directly. <roam uid="VCK0A32IZ"/>
      - Readers of a space don't see who else has access. <roam uid="APgD7Hjar"/>
    - Against: <roam uid="i0NOyj1RW"/>
      - It doesn't replace option A. Ids that were already read stay known, so a known id must be harmless anyway. <roam uid="x7plujA4H"/>
      - It can't be complete. Group members need group ids, and group admins need a way to name members. <roam uid="GICJgztPZ"/>
      - `group_membership` can't use column grants, because shipped plugins filter on `member_id`. <roam uid="T8sJ4q1QP"/>
      - Changing `my_pseudo_accounts` conflicts with ENG-2444, which keeps every view's columns. <roam uid="bT8yfDiON"/>
      - Each new table with a user id needs the same care. <roam uid="JPrKyLLVj"/>
      - Estimated cost: 3 to 4 days on top of option A. <roam uid="qasR_Z5EG"/>
  - Revisit option B if a feature needs a person's user id to stay private from people who share a space or a group with them. <roam uid="3_Cr4tT4b"/>
- Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5" refs="1"/>
  - **Why it matters:** every access policy calls these functions, so they set what each caller reaches and add to the cost of every query. Most of this section is agreed; only the lease length is open. <roam uid="mcAP4xcAU"/>
  - Where the claim lives, without a new table <roam uid="Cq8Z7k1_K"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.dg_account`: the person who claimed the account (exists today). <roam uid="HI27RxILB"/>
    - `PlatformAccount.claim_attestation`: asserted, corroborated, attested, or frozen. <roam uid="LpZMlh92m"/>
    - `LocalAccess.vouched`: this space's session made the claim. <roam uid="Aw4Af4gJG"/>
    - `LocalAccess.last_seen`: the lease. <roam uid="vZYlXEL7h"/>
    - `LocalAccess` admin level and delegated flag: the space-admin decision. <roam uid="p3wczF1ke"/>
    - Each space's pseudo-user uid is needed. Today it is found through the anonymous `PlatformAccount`, whose `account_local_id` is `get_space_anonymous_email(platform, id)`. A `Space.principal_uid` column would be clearer. <roam uid="IRNBzF_Oa"/>
  - Permissions stay in `SpaceAccess`; `LocalAccess` records use and the claim <roam uid="36Yd-0vay"/>
    - `LocalAccess` means a platform account is used in a space. With claims, it also records how strong the claim is (`vouched`, `last_seen`, attestation). <roam uid="_xHiqK5FF"/>
    - Permissions in a space come only from `SpaceAccess`. Claim strength in `LocalAccess` can cap them, but never grant them. <roam uid="vTZOkHOgl"/>
    - Today `LocalAccess` gives the account nothing in the space. It gives the space's members rights over the account: members can read it, and editors can edit or delete it while it is unowned. <roam uid="GyNZ1qUAM"/>
    - Editors need to insert and update those accounts, because they create the platform accounts of authors who may never log in. They don't need to delete them, and dropping delete also removes the cascade through `Document.author_id`. Claiming an account should not be one of those rights: see ((vtxvgZEKp))<ref>Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account</ref>. <roam uid="LhDhvYx-k"/>
  - Open: keeping the claim (`dg_account`) out of ordinary account writes <roam uid="vdV1jigrm" refs="3"/>
    - **Why it matters:** editors must keep writing the platform accounts of their space's authors, but claiming is a separate operation with its own rules. Today any editor of a space can claim its unowned accounts (((vtxvgZEKp))). Not decided; postponed. <roam uid="e3dHDdJ0k"/>
    - Option 1, column privileges: revoke `INSERT` and `UPDATE` on `PlatformAccount` from `authenticated`, then grant them back on every column except `dg_account`. A table-level grant covers all columns, so revoking the one column alone does not work. Cost: each new column has to be added to the grants, and a client upsert that sends `dg_account`, even as null, fails. <roam uid="XbS0B2zbY"/>
    - Option 2, a separate table for the claim: the link between a person and a platform account moves out of `PlatformAccount`, and only the claim path writes it. This departs from "Where the claim lives, without a new table" above. <roam uid="eXQzoqBsj"/>
    - Both options route claims through a `SECURITY DEFINER` claim function that holds the claim rules in one place. If the claim moves later, only the function body changes. The Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` is the only code that sets `dg_account` today, so it would call that function. <roam uid="ftEJrOez4"/>
    - Interim, October 30: `authenticated` can no longer write `dg_account` (column privileges, see ((vtxvgZEKp))<ref>Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account</ref>). Whatever claim mechanism this spec picks starts from there. <roam uid="JfuWa2pWN"/>
  - Three nested sets of uids for a caller <roam uid="mEKDhdnT_"/>
    - `self_to_spaces()`: the caller, plus the spaces the caller acts for through claims (reach rule, lease, not frozen). <roam uid="9DQlyb6HQ"/>
    - `self_to_groups()`: that, plus the groups of every uid in it. One pass over `group_membership`, no recursion. <roam uid="xgb-TmzcC"/>
    - `self_to_everyone()`: that, plus the `everyone` pseudo-user. Replaces `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="p_XEWf7L1"/>
    - These replace `my_user_accounts()` and ENG-1837's `my_identity_accounts()`. Outside SQL, both names only appear in the generated `dbTypes.ts`. <roam uid="25IooWjth"/>
  - Which set each check uses <roam uid="bZ325OCEt"/>
    - Membership and admin checks on a group use `self_to_spaces()`. Groups don't count, otherwise membership would nest. `everyone` never counts. <roam uid="V3mJeIE0I"/>
    - Checks for sharing a space with an account use `self_to_groups()`. A public grant must not count as sharing. <roam uid="_xnlnN4_m"/>
    - Reads use `self_to_everyone()`. <roam uid="XOZ7nL4S6"/>
  - Each set is computed for one principal and works for any caller <roam uid="-7GZXBiOr"/>
    - Space session: the space and its groups, the same as today. <roam uid="INz7A6X98"/>
    - Person: the person, their direct groups, their claimed spaces, and those spaces' groups. <roam uid="9wwDV7p4T"/>
    - Agent: its own expansion, plus the full expansion of its principal from `agent_grant`. <roam uid="pul5mAdGy"/>
  - Group admin <roam uid="GNGlWJVoz"/>
    - Stage 1: `is_group_admin(G)` is true when any uid in `self_to_spaces()` is an admin of G. A person who acts for space S is an admin of G whenever S is. This lets people be promoted to direct group admins without being direct members first. <roam uid="gparhcgzS"/>
    - Stage 2: restrict the space-derived part to people who are admins of S. It waits until space admins exist. <roam uid="ziRKyT9d4"/>
    - The same rule applies to leaving a group: the `group_membership` delete policy would let a person make S leave G. Stage 2 restricts it too. <roam uid="FA4vWPAT2"/>
    - `my_pseudo_accounts` must check `self_to_spaces()` instead of `auth.uid()`. Otherwise a person never sees the groups of their spaces, and publishing to groups finds none. <roam uid="F5fgLmqoL"/>
  - Agreed <roam uid="cCtIzCldr"/>
    - Caps: the sets return each uid with a cap, as `TABLE(uid, cap)` rather than bare uids. Permission checks use the lower of the grant and the cap. A group reached through a capped space inherits the cap. The same mechanism covers read-only access through a space and read-only agents. <roam uid="vLHTviSzs"/>
    - Cost: for a person, each call walks `PlatformAccount`, `LocalAccess`, `Space` and `group_membership`. That is fine once per statement but not once per row, so the RLS rewrite to the `= ANY((SELECT ...))` pattern becomes a prerequisite. <roam uid="SyoGpN9DQ"/>
  - Open: the lease length (90 days is a placeholder). <roam uid="IN5YpaEA5"/>
  - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FoMbD_1Xs-h.svg?alt=media&token=ff8aabdb-be87-480d-932b-ead0847ffe4d) <roam uid="0mR6YMCry"/>
  - {{dg-canvas: [[Canvas/ DG account]]}} <roam uid="fHh1eG1Sn"/>
- Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>
  - Space admin <roam uid="3l40D2TI3"/>
    - **Why it matters:** every admin power is something any holder of the space password can do today, for example rotating that password or joining groups for the space. The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together. <roam uid="YyVfTf1I1"/>
    - Guessed: the plugin reports who is admin. <roam uid="RBdmXSvZj"/>
      - Roam: the plugin reads `roamAlphaAPI.user.isAdmin` ([developer documentation](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/developer-documentation/page/U5DkRU6hr)). It is synchronous, takes no parameters, and answers only for the current user. This replaces the earlier guess, the first user page created in the graph. <roam uid="SdqDeXOxt"/>
        - The plugin can't ask about other users, so an admin is recorded only once that admin runs the plugin. Until then the space has no admin at this tier. <roam uid="xP-d6GZl_"/>
        - To check: the documentation says "an admin of this graph (the graph owner)". Roam graphs can have several admins besides the owner, so it is unclear whether the flag is true for the other admins or only for the owner. <roam uid="2MkuVao0B"/>
      - Obsidian: the only user. <roam uid="L_SdOpU7g"/>
      - Website: the creator of the space. <roam uid="Gbpn8W21T"/>
      - Forgeable on every platform: the plugin sends the report under the space session, so a co-member who holds the space password can report themselves as admin. L8 would prove which Roam user is calling, but not that this user is an admin. In Roam, L6 closes the gap for the admin who supplies a backend token: only admins can create one, and the same token lets our server attest which Roam user they are. That admin moves to the proven tier; other admins stay guessed. <roam uid="yhMBFbag9"/>
    - Registered: the person who first connected the space. Not recorded today. <roam uid="BLTnvtton"/>
    - Proven: whoever supplies a working Roam backend token. Only graph owners and admins can create one. Tokens need an active Roam subscription, so this tier can only override a guess, never be the only way to become admin. <roam uid="9qNvUNN9F"/>
      - Proof without storage: the admin supplies a token, the server checks that it works for this graph, and discards it. <roam uid="mUOuMCo17"/>
      - Proof with storage: the admin agrees to keep the token, which also enables L6 for every member of the graph (see the stored-token variant under L6). <roam uid="2REL1pTdm"/>
      - The token shows that the submitter is an admin. It doesn't say which Roam user they are. The flag should only land on a `PlatformAccount` whose claim is stronger than `asserted`, or the same token should attest the submitter first. <roam uid="U_5nSbh0a"/>
    - How strong the proof must be depends on the list of admin-only powers, which is not defined yet. <roam uid="1Ay60cIYE"/>
    - Leaning: store the admin flag and its strength (guessed, registered, proven) on `LocalAccess`, so a `PlatformAccount` is admin in a space and a person inherits it through their claim. <roam uid="w0bP5wnBY"/>
      - Fits the guessed tier: "the first user page in the graph" names a Roam uid, which is a `PlatformAccount`. <roam uid="6kIjZzHap"/>
      - Several admins per space come for free. Removing the `LocalAccess` row, or letting its lease expire, also removes the admin role. <roam uid="KhfJkTyoB"/>
      - Escalation risk with reach option 2: an `asserted` claim reaches the vouching space. If it also inherits the admin flag of the claimed account, a co-member can assert the admin's uid and become admin. Admin powers should therefore require both an admin flag on `LocalAccess` and a claim stronger than `asserted`. <roam uid="SEhF6UP4l"/>
      - Write protection: today space editors can write `LocalAccess` rows of unclaimed accounts, and owners can write their own. Neither may set the admin flag or its strength. Only a `SECURITY DEFINER` function (or column-level privileges) may write those columns. <roam uid="Ftrn9F8gW"/>
      - A stronger tier doesn't replace weaker admins automatically. An admin interface lets a proven admin demote guessed admins if they choose to. <roam uid="XTmTih6kQ"/>

lastPrompt: Much better reading of generic to specific, and agreed with the ladder as proposed.

- This makes "demote an admin of a weaker tier" the first item on the list of admin-only powers. <roam uid="gSWDdOn6-"/>
        - Open: can an admin demote another admin of the same tier? A rule of "only strictly weaker tiers" stops two guessed admins from removing each other, but leaves no way out of a dispute between them except a stronger proof. <roam uid="x0aFCIehm"/>
    - Admin-only powers <roam uid="gE3hYX534"/>
      - How strong the admin proof must be depends on what admins can do beyond an editor. Today every graph member holds the space password, which acts as editor. <roam uid="fbg0cLP5y"/>
      - Agreed <roam uid="KT6If9giX"/>
        - Demote an admin of a weaker tier. <roam uid="r_FK4G0HP"/>
        - Supply a Roam backend token as proof, and choose whether we keep it. Keeping it is an explicit opt-in. <roam uid="9rNRYMpLf"/>
      - Leaning yes <roam uid="cFJHvwfPG"/>
        - Delete the token we stored, so it no longer exists on our side. (Revoking it in Roam is already up to the admin.) <roam uid="cgzSu3r0V"/>
        - Rotate the space password. Today nothing rotates it, and every past member keeps it. <roam uid="pFQ6fmnbM"/>
        - Join and leave groups on behalf of the space. Today any holder of the space password can accept a group invitation as the space. <roam uid="kx6217H3V"/>
        - Remove a person's access to the space by deleting their `LocalAccess` row, without waiting for the lease to expire. <roam uid="m6ei3fcOi"/>
      - Not an admin power <roam uid="ppu5VG1Sc"/>
        - Approving identity claims (layer L5). Set aside: it feels wrong in general. <roam uid="xoR7fN0tT"/>
        - Setting a policy for cross-space search. The leaning is to always allow it with read access (see "Consent for cross-space search"). <roam uid="T6NbhkV-b"/>
      - Delegate admins (leaning) <roam uid="yt9ViDH2K"/>
        - An admin can name delegate admins, who can use the admin powers even though the platform doesn't see them as admins. <roam uid="JoZfvsjTF"/>
        - Fits `LocalAccess`: a delegate is an admin flag whose level sits just below the delegating admin's level and above the next level down. Who delegated is not recorded. <roam uid="ndH91oosF"/>
          - Resulting order, weakest first: guessed-delegated, guessed, registered-delegated, registered, proven-delegated, proven. <roam uid="hjfsHe13t"/>
          - Two ways to store it: a six-value level, or the three tiers plus a `delegated` flag, compared on the tier first and then with delegated below non-delegated. They give the same order. <roam uid="PXUtvwxz6"/>
          - With the demotion rule (only strictly lower levels), a delegate of a proven admin can demote registered and guessed admins, but not the proven admin who named them. <roam uid="HJXkL5XUj"/>
        - A delegate can name further delegates, at the delegate's own level. Delegates at the same level can't demote each other. This keeps the system simple, which suits small teams. <roam uid="IPvSBnYxB"/>
        - A delegation doesn't end on its own when the admin who made it is demoted or leaves. Whoever demotes an admin also decides about the remaining delegates. <roam uid="S2wcRkuYG"/>
      - Each candidate moved to admins takes a power away from "anyone with the space password". Each one also raises the bar for the admin proof. <roam uid="TPTTRkHSH"/>
  - Personal session in the plugins <roam uid="v-wdJK626"/>
    - **Why it matters:** this sets how a person logs in from a plugin, and where the plugin keeps that login. In Roam, keeping the login across reloads exposes it to every other extension, and not keeping it costs a click after each reload. It also decides which work runs as the person and which as the space, because some functions break if the person replaces the space. <roam uid="XtAl_AlUO"/>
    - Delivery: leaning towards Supabase Auth acting as an OAuth server, with the plugin as an OAuth client (PKCE). The person logs in on the Website by whatever method their account uses, so password accounts work too. Fallback: a device-style flow over `secret_token`, where the plugin opens the Website and then polls for the session. <roam uid="anOlv9O2J"/>
      - The Supabase OAuth 2.1 Server has no separate charge. People who sign in through it count toward the project's monthly active users, like any other sign-in. Source: Supabase docs, OAuth 2.1 Server guide. Accepted as an added cost. <roam uid="Z6B0tGor7"/>
      - Completing the flow inside the plugin is nice to have, not required. If it can't, the flow completes in a browser tab: the Website receives the result and the plugin collects it through the `secret_token` fallback. <roam uid="HmGIe3SsJ"/>
      - Social login (Supabase `signInWithOAuth` and identity linking) is a separate need on the Website: adding external identities to an account, and logging in with them. <roam uid="THBV37Ayp"/>
      - A person may create their account with an external identity and keep logging in with it, without ever setting a password. The plugin flow works the same for them, because the login step happens on the Website. <roam uid="IrbMTsSJY"/>
      - External identities linked this way are verified by their provider, so they can also serve as trusted identifiers for attribution. ORCID is not a built-in provider (ENG-405). <roam uid="MtQhgD_oh"/>
    - Storage: never in graph settings or the vault's `data.json`, which other people can read or sync. In Roam, `localStorage` is shared with every extension. <roam uid="jQDFzycLX"/>
      - Supabase sets token lifetimes: the access token expires after the project's JWT expiry (one hour by default), and the refresh token lasts until it is used, revoked, or cut off by a session time-box or inactivity timeout, if the project sets one. <roam uid="sggTyBNKs"/>
      - These settings apply to the whole project, including Website sessions, not only to the plugins. <roam uid="qppZbZExq"/>
      - What the plugin decides is whether it keeps the refresh token: <roam uid="VNhkLUpxm"/>
        - Kept in `localStorage`: the session survives reloads, but any Roam extension can read the refresh token and act as the person. <roam uid="KiIUY_QsL"/>
        - Kept in memory only: the session ends at each page reload, and the plugin runs the OAuth flow again. <roam uid="6h1qgZaHl"/>
      - Re-running the flow is cheap: the Website keeps its own login cookie on its own origin, which Roam extensions can't read. If the person is still logged in on the Website, the flow completes without typing anything. <roam uid="Rnxg83ODf"/>
      - Roam never reads the Website's cookie. The plugin opens a popup on the Website, the popup uses the cookie to skip the login form, and the Website sends an authorization code back to the plugin's page. The plugin exchanges the code for its own tokens, separate from the Website's session. <roam uid="D7aP7KN83"/>
      - A popup needs a user click, so after a reload the person clicks once to reconnect. A hidden iframe could avoid the click, but browsers increasingly block the cookies it would need. <roam uid="z-uzA5aW1"/>
      - Memory-only storage stops theft of tokens at rest. It doesn't stop a malicious extension that is running in the same page while the session is active, for example by wrapping `fetch`. <roam uid="OAS1AAkJ6"/>
      - Pending: keep tokens in memory in Roam (one click to reconnect after each reload), or keep the refresh token in `localStorage` (no click, but other extensions can steal it). Obsidian can store tokens on disk outside the vault either way. <roam uid="5YETQsAFC"/>
    - Two sessions: the plugin keeps the space session and adds a personal session when one is available. <roam uid="A8N_Jsvr1"/>
      - Downsides of switching the plugin from the space session to the personal session when one is available <roam uid="esLlHtygy"/>
        - Reads are equivalent or wider: the person sees their space, plus every other space and group they reach. That is what cross-space search needs. <roam uid="ckoj72WSx"/>
        - Some functions use `auth.uid()` to mean "the space", so their behavior changes with a personal session: <roam uid="RwmJfxu2_"/>
          - `accept_group_invitation` adds `auth.uid()` to the group. With a personal session, the person joins the group instead of the space. That breaks the rule that a space is shared with a group only while the space's pseudo-user is a member. <roam uid="hpKF4x5Cr"/>
          - `my_pseudo_accounts` finds groups through `auth.uid()` being a member. A person who isn't a direct member sees no groups, so publishing to groups (`getPublishedGroupIdsByRid`) finds none. <roam uid="ZTcuCO_P6"/>
          - `upsert_account_in_space` writes a `SpaceAccess` row for any account whose `dg_account` is set. Once claims set `dg_account`, it would copy grants to the person, which option A ruled out. The branch has to go. <roam uid="0RzabN3lg"/>
        - Code that relies on RLS to keep results inside the current space would start returning other spaces' content. Plugin queries should filter by space explicitly. Not audited yet. <roam uid="g9oBrenl5"/>
        - The personal session can disappear in the middle of work: it is short-lived in Roam, its lease can expire, and a claim can be frozen by conflict detection. Sync must fall back to the space session without failing. <roam uid="c6U6CEgwk"/>
        - Each query pays for a larger `my_user_accounts()` set. This only matters for people in many spaces. <roam uid="4dMwUYBr6"/>
        - The space session can't be dropped: creating the space and acting as the space with groups still need it. <roam uid="-Mq1IUscM"/>
      - Split: the personal session for reads, search and actions done as the person; the space session for sync, group membership and sharing. <roam uid="OhtCf8HO2"/>
  - Consent for cross-space search <roam uid="fi-J8nr1F"/>
    - Today content crosses spaces only through a group both spaces joined. Search from the plugin lets a person bridge two spaces that never agreed. <roam uid="EUEJ5yT3O"/>
    - Options: a member's read access is enough, or each space sets a policy for being searched from other spaces. Leaning: read access is enough, with no space policy. <roam uid="cuMNT218A"/>
    - Cost of the leaning: a member of a private graph B can find B's content while working in graph A and import it into A. They could already copy it by hand, but the tool makes it routine, and B has no say. <roam uid="XhscC1bBd"/>
  - Personal information before consent (ENG-918) <roam uid="sPWWnb1Zg"/>
    - **Why it matters:** the plugins already store the names and emails of people who never agreed to it. This decides what other users can see of them, and how same-named people are told apart. <roam uid="ukHWWQ9Zr"/>
    - Plugins create `PlatformAccount` rows with names and emails before the person has agreed to anything. <roam uid="f_HUcUaFh"/>
    - Options: keep sending, hold names and emails until a link exists, or mask by default (as ENG-1837 does with `anonymous #<id>`). <roam uid="w5NITWyZl"/>
    - Leaning: expose names, and keep emails hidden until the person shares them explicitly. Emails are stored in any case. Same-named people are told apart by showing the name with the `PlatformAccount` id. <roam uid="xu0Zrp-lp"/>
      - This is about exposure, not storage. The plugins still send emails: identity layer L1 needs the stored email to check the uid-to-email binding. Only the person and server-side functions read it. <roam uid="b-WXuL0SL"/>
      - Cost: names aren't unique. Two people in a space can share a name, and imports across spaces can't tell same-named authors apart. <roam uid="5PDfzx8LK"/>
      - Ways to tell same-named people apart without emails: <roam uid="HrdY6jxk0"/>
        - Show the name with the `PlatformAccount` id, as ENG-1837 already does for `anonymous #<id>`. A Roam uid has one `PlatformAccount` in every graph, so the id also matches the same Roam user across spaces. Cheap, but not pretty. <roam uid="gZFaAP3K8"/>
        - Give claimed personal accounts a unique handle, chosen by the person. Unclaimed accounts keep the name and id. <roam uid="-pTyhBAKq"/>
        - An opaque id per person, computed on the server from the email with a secret salt. It is stable and unique, and doesn't reveal the email. Plain email hashes are not safe, because emails can be guessed. <roam uid="Rj_nty-bD"/>
      - Once an account is claimed, the profile name is shown, because it is the name most directly under the person's control. <roam uid="oXvuGtrd3"/>
  - Profile visibility <roam uid="S4MegNHAq"/>
    - Options: a visibility value per field, or access rows per field and audience in the style of `ResourceAccess`, with `everyone`, a group or shared-space peers as the audience. <roam uid="1HwtriyvB"/>
    - FEE-755 set the minimum profile to name and email, with ORCID later. <roam uid="2We7q8coS"/>
    - Leaning: one row per person and audience, in the style of `ResourceAccess`, holding an array of visible fields. <roam uid="lM4axaive"/>
      - The audience is a principal uid: `everyone`, a group, or a space pseudo-user. A space as audience means everyone who acts for that space, which fits the access model above. <roam uid="fYeVpSrjI"/>
      - A viewer usually belongs to several audiences, so the visible fields are the union of the arrays of every row whose audience is in the viewer's `my_user_accounts()`. <roam uid="NECKklm5j"/>
      - Compared with one row per field: fewer rows and one write per audience. The field names in the array need a check against the allowed set, since a foreign key can't do it. <roam uid="1jrgL3Jdh"/>
  - Which accounts a caller can see <roam uid="aY4D_LNku"/>
    - **Why it matters:** `my_accounts` shows every account of every space where the caller has `partial` access, not only the people behind content the caller can read.     - Today: an account shows when it is tied through `LocalAccess` to a space where the caller has at least `partial` access. Accounts that the caller reaches only through a public grant show as `anonymous #<id>`. <roam uid="3kKS5i-_j"/>
    - Option: show only the authors and contributors of resources the caller can read. <roam uid="wt7Xr-Yn9"/>
      - For: a reader learns only who made what they can see. An account with no published work stays hidden. <roam uid="4V_S5pKVG"/>
      - Cost: each check goes through the content and contributor tables instead of the space, so it costs more than today's space check. <roam uid="bgJq97ROb"/>

    - No personal account. This is the default for most Roam users, and it stays a supported state. <roam uid="eYMhqxGzH"/>
    - Personal account, but this platform account isn't claimed. <roam uid="Bjrnaea-R"/>
    - Claimed, `asserted`: the claim reaches only the vouching space. <roam uid="k2D08bJR0"/>

    - Claim frozen by conflict detection (L3). <roam uid="HRr5cLTIP"/>
    - Claimed by a different personal account than the one signed in on this device. <roam uid="SZ2LB-uMd"/>
    - Personal session lost: page reload with memory-only storage, refresh token revoked, or lease expired. <roam uid="X4c9EjIG3"/>
    - Admin level in this space (guessed, registered, proven, each with a delegated level), and whether the claim is strong enough to use it. <roam uid="HSXtIQz5W"/>

    - Status indicator: always visible, shows the space session and the personal session, the account name, and the claim level. Roam: settings panel and maybe a topbar icon. Obsidian: status bar and settings tab. <roam uid="Z4UqWZAPa"/>
    - First run: offers to connect a personal account, and says plainly that skipping it loses nothing the plugin does today. <roam uid="VrFInrgPn"/>
    - Connect and reconnect: the button that opens the Website popup (OAuth with PKCE), or the browser tab of the `secret_token` fallback. In Roam with memory-only storage, a "Reconnect" prompt after each reload. <roam uid="HkrF-tl7R"/>
    - OAuth consent screen on the Website: names the plugin and the space that asks to act as the person. <roam uid="5y78Mallc"/>
    - Cross-space search <roam uid="22t6V1Bln"/>
      - Without a personal session, results cover this space and its groups only. The search UI says so and offers to sign in. <roam uid="uP9dAamDv"/>
      - With `asserted` claims, results cover only the spaces the person connected one by one. The UI lists the spaces searched, and says how to add others (open the plugin there, or prove identity). <roam uid="Zv4YUFGaZ"/>
      - A space whose lease expired drops out of results without notice unless the UI lists it. <roam uid="iOb9sr7DM"/>
      - Each result shows its source space, so the person knows where an import would come from. <roam uid="cUFogcFJe"/>

The OpenSpec change `agent-read-only-access` (read-only Supabase access for AI agents) finished planning on 2026-09-16. All four artifacts are in `openspec/changes/agent-read-only-access/` and pass `openspec validate --strict`. **Implementation has not started.** The user starts it with `/opsx:apply`.

**Where it lives.** The user pasted the artifacts into Roam as [OpenSpec/Agent read-only access](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/DHOqLFwkT). Top-level block UIDs: Spec `OHfAX-ANr`, Proposal `wo1G9LSI9`, Design `xzNpL58c4`, Tasks `h_Lgn1Ro0`. The broader context (identity, read-only tokens, writing agents) is in block [-Q3X_phzD](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/-Q3X_phzD), a TODO for Joel Chan. Direct Roam writes work since 2026-10-23 (see [[roam-propose-write-quirks]]); keep the local files and the page in step by hand. The user doesn't plan to commit the local files; Roam is the home.

**2026-10-31 changes (in both copies):**
- "Alternative to consider: a restricted session of the principal, without an agent user" section after Migration Plan (Roam Eg4aD33rW). The hook gives one registered session of the principal `agent_reader`. Explicitly **not a decision**; still being weighed against decision 1. Trade: immediate revocation and separate identity vs fewer moving parts.
- New risk: Edge Functions write with the service key, so the role doesn't stop them (Roam YF7DRHmiF). Mitigation is a shared caller check. **No task added**: the tasks describe the original design while the choice is open.
- The grant requirement now reads "a logged-in (non-agent) user" (the user's edit).
- Trang Doan's question (VgqKSYHkc) was answered by the user: agents are identified by `role`, and more generally by joining `agent_grant.agent_id`. The column name isn't fixed in the design yet.

**Decisions the user settled, and that should not be reopened:**
- **Agent identity.** Each grant creates its own auth user with `auth.users.role = 'agent_reader'`, set through `auth.admin.createUser({ role })`. Supabase Auth reapplies that role to every token it issues. Self-signed JWTs were rejected: asymmetric keys, and a password-reset escalation when `sub` is the principal.
- **Delegation.** An `agent_grant` row maps the agent to its principal, and `my_user_accounts()` adds the principal and the principal's groups. No access rows are copied, and the 18 direct `auth.uid()` checks stay as they are. The user first worried this copied rows into `group_membership`. It does not, because the function only reads the principal's memberships.
- **Enforcement.** Grants enforce read-only, not RLS.
- **Function execution.** `EXECUTE` is revoked from `PUBLIC` globally. The user first wanted this per function, then agreed global is safer. Every function already has explicit `anon`, `authenticated`, and `service_role` grants, checked in `pg_proc`, so anonymous reads (ENG-1837) and `create-space` are unaffected.
- **Where grant management runs.** A Supabase Edge Function `create-agent` (like `create-group`), plus RPC and RLS for listing and revoking. There is no Vercel endpoint. The UI is on the website under `auth/`, not in the plugins.
- **What the grant holds.** No expiry and no permission column. Writing agents (future) get `role: authenticated`, and the access they inherit is capped with `SpaceAccessPermissions`. Finer operation kinds become extra Postgres roles.
- **Agent email domain.** `agents.discoursegraphs.com`.

**Overlap with ENG-1837** (PR #1106, public resources). It also edits `my_user_accounts()`, so whichever change lands second must keep both edits.

The converter from the OpenSpec files to a Roam outline was a session scratchpad script and is gone. Rebuild it from the page's layout if needed: plain heading blocks; each scenario is a sibling of its requirement, with WHEN and THEN as children; tasks are `{{[[TODO]]}}` blocks.

Related: [[openspec-cli-location]], [[write-for-cold-readers]].

**2026-11-02 restructure:** the alternative section now opens with "Summary for planning" (Roam QwvJD7vqp), written for a moderately technical project manager, and collapses details under "Technical notes" (cZZWH-4iZ). The user holds that a v0 baseline of full access and no revocation is acceptable. Effort there is stepped: v0 baseline, then revocation plus password settings immediately after v0 (about 1.25 days, same for both), then read-only (session 3.5–4.5 days, agent-user 6–9). The from-zero comparison (5–7 vs 6–9) stays in the technical table.

As of 2026-10-31: OpenSpec change `openspec/changes/mcp-space-session-handoff/` drafted; its home is Roam page kPg_0_-lh ("Spec: MCP token handoff"; top blocks Proposal NZMOpbT2i, Spec GYtOqf4U2, Design -0hMsmA6D, Tasks Dw-EclQK6). First target is per-space platform accounts.

**v0 design:** plugin opens a second, non-persisting, non-refreshing client session and hands the MCP a bundle (URL, anon key, space ID, refresh token only). The session registers itself in `mcp_session` (session_id from `auth.jwt()`, FK to `auth.sessions` ON DELETE CASCADE). Follow-up per-session sign-out = SECURITY DEFINER delete from `auth.sessions` for registered sessions only. MCP can sign out with local scope; `signOut others` is the emergency switch. Full space-account permissions in v0.

**Settled by the user 2026-10-31:** dedicated session (not long-lived JWT, password, or OAuth 2.1 server — its consent page would need the space password typed in a browser); every plugin user may connect (admin check would only hide the command); `secure_password_change` on AND "require current password" on (hosted only); keep `mcp_session` and registration in v0 even if sign-out is postponed, because unregistered sessions can't be identified later.

**Open, needs a group decision (not the user alone):** whether per-session sign-out and the password settings stay out of v0. Proposed 2026-11-02: both immediately after v0 (task group 5, about 1.25 days in one app), since full access without revocation is held to be an acceptable baseline. NOT settled; the user corrected this when I wrote it as settled. Table and registration ship in v0 either way. No Linear tickets yet; task groups are the proposed ticket boundaries.

**Why:** the user wants v0 MCP access soon; read-only accounts post-v0. **How to apply:** Roam is the home of both specs; the user does not plan to commit the local OpenSpec files. Keep local copies in sync by hand when either changes. Supabase facts behind the design: [[supabase-auth-session-facts]]. Related: [[agent-read-only-access-state]].

content.text: I've read the whole spec page, plus my notes on agent access and v0. Next I'm drafting the ladder section in a local file so you can review it before anything goes to Roam.

input.content:
- Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it
  - **Why it matters:** the rest of this page describes the long-term design. The first release of personal accounts will be much smaller: almost certainly no claim checking beyond the space session, and probably no Roam sign-in token (L8). This section says what that release contains, which steps can follow, and what each step buys in security or in features, so the group can choose the order.
  - "Accounts v0" means the first release of personal accounts. It is not the product v0, which is done.
  - Proposed accounts v0
    - A person creates a Discourse Graphs account on the Website, with a password or a built-in social login (Google, GitHub).
    - The person connects a platform account from the plugin. The only evidence is the space session that made the claim (L0), so every claim is `asserted`.
    - Reach follows option 2: an `asserted` claim reaches only the vouching space. To reach several spaces, the person connects once from each of them.
    - The plugin keeps the space session for sync, groups and sharing, and adds a personal session for reads and search.
    - Open: how the plugin gets the personal session. The `secret_token` handoff reuses the existing `auth/token` route. The OAuth 2.1 server is the long-term leaning, but adds a consent page and client setup.
    - Website: a sign-in banner, and an account page that lists the claimed platform accounts and the spaces they reach.
    - Plugins: a status indicator, connect and reconnect, and cross-space search over the connected spaces.
    - Not in v0: attribution export, space admin tiers, agents acting for a person, profile visibility settings beyond "name shown, email hidden".
  - What v0 buys
    - Cross-space search inside the plugins, over every space the person connected, without an ad-hoc group.
    - Login on the Website as a person, without going through a plugin.
    - People, not only spaces, as direct group admins (stage 1 under "Group admin").
    - Security stays where it is today: a forged claim reaches only a space whose password the forger already holds.
  - What v0 still allows
    - Any co-member can claim another member's platform account in that space. They gain no access they didn't have, but the name and the account page now show them as that member.
    - Open: what happens when a second person claims an account that is already claimed. Without conflict detection (L3) the first claim wins, so a co-member can block the real owner. One way out in v0: a new claim replaces the old one. That stops blocking, but lets two people take the account back and forth.
    - Consequence for names: an `asserted` claim doesn't show who made it. Showing the profile name of whoever claimed an account would let a co-member rename another member's work. Until a stronger step lands, v0 should keep showing the platform name.
  - Prerequisites for v0
    - Close the `group_membership` insert hole: done (ENG-2438).
    - Route claims through one claim function, outside ordinary account writes (ENG-2447).
    - Remove the branch of `upsert_account_in_space` that copies grants to a claimed account.
    - Evaluate access sets once per query, not once per row (ENG-2443).
    - Replace `my_user_accounts()` with the three nested sets (`self_to_spaces()`, `self_to_groups()`, `self_to_everyone()`).
  - Steps after v0
    - These can come in any order, except where a step names what it needs.
    - Conflict detection and notification (L3)
      - Adds: a mail when an account is linked, a check on plugin load ("Was this you?"), and frozen claims while a conflict is settled.
      - Buys security: a forged claim is noticed and can be reversed. It also gives the blocked owner a way out.
      - Cost: low to medium. Needs a verified email on the personal account.
    - Email binding (L1)
      - Adds: a claim becomes `attested` when the personal account controls the email that Roam records for the platform account.
      - Buys features: reach widens to every space of that platform account, without connecting each one. Attribution becomes possible.
      - Buys security: stops a co-member who can't falsify where the binding comes from.
      - Cost: low. Roam only until we know whether the Obsidian plugin can read a verified email.
    - Corroboration (L2)
      - Adds: a claim becomes `corroborated` when two or more spaces recorded the same account details before the claim.
      - Buys features: the same wider reach, with no effort, for people in two or more graphs.
      - Buys security: stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs.
      - Cost: low, a query over existing rows.
    - Attribution
      - Adds: the profile name shown for claims above `asserted`, `prov:wasAttributedTo` in the export, and verified identifiers such as ORCID.
      - Buys features: one author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website.
      - Needs: email binding or corroboration, or a stronger proof.
    - Space admin tiers and admin-only powers
      - Adds: guessed, registered and proven admins on `LocalAccess`, and powers such as rotating the space password, joining and leaving groups, and removing a person's access.
      - Buys security: each power moved to admins is taken away from everyone who holds the space password.
      - Needs: claims above `asserted`, or a co-member could assert the admin's account and become admin.
    - Per-device keys (L4)
      - Buys security: prevents forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run, including people with no personal account.
      - Cost: medium, and new-device prompts for users.
    - Roam backend token (L6)
      - Adds: an optional proof, per person or stored per graph by an admin.
      - Buys security: no forgery for the people it covers. It also gives the proven admin tier.
      - Cost: medium once, high if we store tokens. Needs a Roam subscription.
    - Roam sign-in token (L8)
      - Buys security: no forgery for every Roam user, with no effort.
      - Blocked: Roam's terms of service and Roam's agreement. Unlikely.
    - Agents acting for a person
      - Adds: an agent reads what its person reads, as a restricted session of that person rather than a separate principal.
      - Buys features: the agent follows the person's reach as it grows.
    - Profile visibility per audience
      - Adds: the person chooses which fields the public, each group, and shared-space peers see.
      - Matters once attribution shows profile names.
    - Website-native contribution
      - Adds: a personal space on the `Website` platform for proposed nodes, connected to published nodes through cross-space relations.

- Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it
  - **Why it matters:** the rest of this page describes the long-term design. The first release of personal accounts will be much smaller: almost certainly no claim checking beyond the space session, and probably no Roam sign-in token (L8). This section says what that release contains, which steps can follow, and what each step buys in security or in features, so the group can choose the order.
  - "Accounts v0" means the first release of personal accounts. It is not the product v0, which is done.
  - Proposed accounts v0
    - A person creates a Discourse Graphs account on the Website, with a password or a built-in social login (Google, GitHub).
    - The person connects a platform account from the plugin. The only evidence is the space session that made the claim (L0), so every claim is `asserted`.
    - Reach follows option 2: an `asserted` claim reaches only the vouching space. To reach several spaces, the person connects once from each of them.
    - The plugin keeps the space session for sync, groups and sharing, and adds a personal session for reads and search.
    - Open: how the plugin gets the personal session. The `secret_token` handoff reuses the existing `auth/token` route. The OAuth 2.1 server is the long-term leaning, but adds a consent page and client setup.
    - Website: a sign-in banner, and an account page that lists the claimed platform accounts and the spaces they reach.
    - Plugins: a status indicator, connect and reconnect, and cross-space search over the connected spaces.
    - Not in v0: attribution export, space admin tiers, agents acting for a person, profile visibility settings beyond "name shown, email hidden".
  - What v0 buys
    - Cross-space search inside the plugins, over every space the person connected, without an ad-hoc group.
    - Login on the Website as a person, without going through a plugin.
    - People, not only spaces, as direct group admins (stage 1 under "Group admin").
    - Security stays where it is today: a forged claim reaches only a space whose password the forger already holds.
  - What v0 still allows
    - Any co-member can claim another member's platform account in that space. They gain no access they didn't have, but the name and the account page now show them as that member.
    - Open: what happens when a second person claims an account that is already claimed. Without conflict detection (L3) the first claim wins, so a co-member can block the real owner. One way out in v0: a new claim replaces the old one. That stops blocking, but lets two people take the account back and forth.
    - Consequence for names: an `asserted` claim doesn't show who made it. Showing the profile name of whoever claimed an account would let a co-member rename another member's work. Until a stronger step lands, v0 should keep showing the platform name.
  - Prerequisites for v0
    - Close the `group_membership` insert hole: done (ENG-2438).
    - Route claims through one claim function, outside ordinary account writes (ENG-2447).
    - Remove the branch of `upsert_account_in_space` that copies grants to a claimed account.
    - Evaluate access sets once per query, not once per row (ENG-2443).
    - Replace `my_user_accounts()` with the three nested sets (`self_to_spaces()`, `self_to_groups()`, `self_to_everyone()`).
  - Steps after v0
    - These can come in any order, except where a step names what it needs.
    - Conflict detection and notification (L3)
      - Adds: a mail when an account is linked, a check on plugin load ("Was this you?"), and frozen claims while a conflict is settled.
      - Buys security: a forged claim is noticed and can be reversed. It also gives the blocked owner a way out.
      - Cost: low to medium. Needs a verified email on the personal account.
    - Email binding (L1)
      - Adds: a claim becomes `attested` when the personal account controls the email that Roam records for the platform account.
      - Buys features: reach widens to every space of that platform account, without connecting each one. Attribution becomes possible.
      - Buys security: stops a co-member who can't falsify where the binding comes from.
      - Cost: low. Roam only until we know whether the Obsidian plugin can read a verified email.
    - Corroboration (L2)
      - Adds: a claim becomes `corroborated` when two or more spaces recorded the same account details before the claim.
      - Buys features: the same wider reach, with no effort, for people in two or more graphs.
      - Buys security: stops a forger who is in only one of the victim's graphs.
      - Cost: low, a query over existing rows.
    - Attribution
      - Adds: the profile name shown for claims above `asserted`, `prov:wasAttributedTo` in the export, and verified identifiers such as ORCID.
      - Buys features: one author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website.
      - Needs: email binding or corroboration, or a stronger proof.
    - Space admin tiers and admin-only powers
      - Adds: guessed, registered and proven admins on `LocalAccess`, and powers such as rotating the space password, joining and leaving groups, and removing a person's access.
      - Buys security: each power moved to admins is taken away from everyone who holds the space password.
      - Needs: claims above `asserted`, or a co-member could assert the admin's account and become admin.
    - Per-device keys (L4)
      - Buys security: prevents forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run, including people with no personal account.
      - Cost: medium, and new-device prompts for users.
    - Roam backend token (L6)
      - Adds: an optional proof, per person or stored per graph by an admin.
      - Buys security: no forgery for the people it covers. It also gives the proven admin tier.
      - Cost: medium once, high if we store tokens. Needs a Roam subscription.
    - Roam sign-in token (L8)
      - Buys security: no forgery for every Roam user, with no effort.
      - Blocked: Roam's terms of service and Roam's agreement. Unlikely.
    - Agents acting for a person
      - Adds: an agent reads what its person reads, as a restricted session of that person rather than a separate principal.
      - Buys features: the agent follows the person's reach as it grows.
    - Profile visibility per audience
      - Adds: the person chooses which fields the public, each group, and shared-space peers see.
      - Matters once attribution shows profile names.
    - Website-native contribution
      - Adds: a personal space on the `Website` platform for proposed nodes, connected to published nodes through cross-space relations.

{"uid":"5cTXWhzAt","markdown":"- Require editor access to a space before adding accounts to it <roam uid="5cTXWhzAt" heading="1" refs="8"/>
  - [ENG-2439: Require editor access to a space before adding accounts to it​](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2439/require-editor-access-to-a-space-before-adding-accounts-to-it) <roam uid="GPesHlfiT" refs="1"/>
  - Need / Problem Statement <roam uid="1jHL1QXBq"/>
    - What is the problem that you are trying to solve? <roam uid="f5EqE3XRJ"/>
      - The problem is: any caller, logged in or not, can change accounts in any space without access to it. They call `upsert_account_in_space` with that space's id and an account's `account_local_id`. Nothing checks that they have access to the space. <roam uid="q4a8xotgj"/>
      - `upsert_account_in_space` (`supabase/schemas/account.sql`) adds an account to a space. It upserts the `PlatformAccount` row and adds `LocalAccess` and `AgentIdentifier` rows. If the account has an owner (`dg_account`), it also adds a `SpaceAccess` row for that owner. It is `SECURITY DEFINER`, so it skips row-level security on all four tables. <roam uid="p_A8BRYXP"/>
      - `create_account_in_space` and `upsert_accounts_in_space` call it and have the same problem. <roam uid="8qkwPVtqD"/>
      - For an account without an owner, the caller can do three things: rename the `PlatformAccount`, link it to the space through `LocalAccess`, and add email identifiers to it. <roam uid="OlbzLUsly"/>
      - For an account with an owner, the function currently fails with an error, so the call changes nothing. The branch that adds `SpaceAccess` has two bugs: a `COALESCE` that mixes `SpaceAccessPermissions` with `text`, and a call to `my_permissions_in_space` without the `public.` schema under `search_path = ''`. <roam uid="zWwzflSjU"/>
      - Those bugs are the only thing that stops a privilege escalation. If they were fixed, a caller could give an account they own editor access to any space. The cap on the new row, `least(my_permissions_in_space(space_id_), 'editor')`, does not stop this: `my_permissions_in_space` returns NULL when the caller has no access, and `LEAST` ignores NULL, so the result is `editor`. <roam uid="O3CGol4HA"/>
      - The branch should not exist. `LocalAccess` says that an account belongs to a space and gives no permission. `SpaceAccess` gives permission, and today only groups and a space's own account hold it. People will get `SpaceAccess` through their Discourse Graphs account, after the account verification planned for that. Granting it here, because an editor listed the person as an author, would bypass that verification. <roam uid="Ep0sYtDP4"/>
    - Who is affected? What are they trying to do, and what is stopping them? <roam uid="6XQKf7rHx"/>
      - Every space with accounts that have no owner, which today includes most person accounts, such as the authors listed in a Roam graph. Anyone who knows an account's `account_local_id` can change its name and identifiers. <roam uid="MFiGcL_Ze"/>
    - What request, observation, or other evidence supports this? <roam uid="qXJamvajG"/>
      - Found by reading the schema while documenting the Supabase security warnings ([[[[Supabase]] Warnings]], ENG-2436). <roam uid="SencBB3i9"/>
      - Reproduced on a local database, in a transaction that was rolled back: as the `anon` role, `upsert_account_in_space` renamed an unowned `PlatformAccount` and added an email identifier to it. <roam uid="4A0-8FVw3"/>
      - Reproduced the same way: for an account with an owner, the call fails with `COALESCE types public."SpaceAccessPermissions" and text cannot be matched`. With that fixed, the next error is `function my_permissions_in_space(...) does not exist`. <roam uid="CttAnjfm0"/>
      - Verified on the local test database: `anon` and `authenticated` both have EXECUTE on `upsert_account_in_space`, `upsert_accounts_in_space` and `create_account_in_space` (`has_function_privilege`). <roam uid="yWpYe1ngO"/>
      - Verified on the local test database: `SELECT least(NULL::text, 'editor')` returns `editor`. <roam uid="aiAPch8cs"/>
  - Proposed approach <roam uid="_rfvyEhhv"/>

input.content:
- Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it
  - **Why it matters:** the rest of this page describes the long-term design. The first release of personal accounts will be much smaller: almost certainly no strong proof of identity, and probably nothing that depends on Roam's own login. This section says what that release contains, which steps can follow, and what each step buys in security or in features, so the group can choose the order.
  - "Accounts v0" means the first release of personal accounts. It is not the product v0, which is done.
  - Weak and strong claims
    - When a person connects a platform account from a plugin, they claim "this platform account is me".
    - In v0 every claim is weak: the only evidence is that it came from someone using that space. Any co-member could have made it.
    - A strong claim comes with a proof that a co-member can't fake. Each step below that adds a proof turns some weak claims into strong ones.
    - The question for each stage is how far a weak claim reaches, and what a co-member gains by forging one.
  - Proposed accounts v0
    - A person creates a Discourse Graphs account on the Website, with a password or a common social login such as Google or GitHub.
    - The person connects their platform account from the plugin, once per space, or more widely (see "Open: how far a weak claim reaches in v0").
    - The plugin keeps acting as the space for sync, groups and sharing. It acts as the person for reads and search.
    - Website: a banner that says who is signed in, and an account page that lists the connected platform accounts and the spaces they reach.
    - Plugins: an indicator of who the plugin acts as, a button to connect or reconnect, and search across the person's spaces.
    - Open: how the plugin gets the person's login. A one-time token handed from the plugin to the Website is the simplest. A standard login flow (OAuth) is the long-term leaning, but needs a consent page and more setup.
    - Not in v0: attribution, space admins, agents acting for a person, and visibility settings beyond "name shown, email hidden".
  - Open: how far a weak claim reaches in v0
    - Narrow: only the space where the claim was made.
      - A forger gains nothing: they already act as that space.
      - Cost: the person connects from each space before search covers it.
    - Wider, read-only: also every other space where the same platform account appears, for reading only.
      - The person connects once, and search covers all their spaces.
      - A forger can read the victim's other spaces. In Roam, a person often belongs to several graphs, so this is a real leak.
    - Wider, full: the same reach, with the same permissions the platform account has there.
      - A forger can act in the victim's other spaces.
    - Whatever v0 allows can tighten later, once strong claims exist: weak claims would fall back to a narrower reach. People then lose access they had, so a wider v0 reach should be announced as temporary.
  - What v0 buys
    - Search inside the plugins across the person's spaces, without creating a group just for that.
    - Login on the Website as a person, without going through a plugin.
    - People, not only spaces, as group admins.
    - Security: with the narrow reach, no change from today. With a wider reach, the leak described above.
  - What v0 still allows
    - Any co-member can claim another member's platform account. With the narrow reach they gain no access, but the account page shows them as that member.
    - Open: what happens when a second person claims an account that is already claimed. If the first claim wins, a co-member can block the real owner. If the newest claim wins, two people can take the account back and forth.
    - Names: a weak claim doesn't show who made it. If the claimant's profile name replaced the platform name, a co-member could rename another member's work. Until strong claims exist, v0 should keep showing the platform name.
  - Steps after v0
    - These can come in any order, except where a step names what it needs.
    - Notify and detect conflicts
      - Adds: a mail when an account is connected, a check when the plugin starts ("Was this you?"), and a hold on claims that conflict until someone settles them.
      - Buys security: a forged claim is noticed fast and can be reversed. It also gives a blocked owner a way out.
      - Needs: a verified email on the personal account.
    - Match the email
      - Adds: a claim becomes strong when the person's account controls the email that the platform records for the platform account.
      - Buys features: the claim reaches all the person's spaces at once. Attribution becomes possible.
      - Buys security: stops a co-member who can't fake the platform's email record.
      - Limit: Roam only, until we know whether Obsidian exposes a verified email.
    - Agreement between spaces
      - Adds: a claim becomes strong when two or more spaces recorded the same account details before the claim.
      - Buys features: the same wider reach, with no effort, for people in several graphs.
      - Buys security: stops a forger who shares only one graph with the victim.
    - Attribution
      - Adds: the person's chosen name on their work, attribution in the export, and verified identifiers such as ORCID.
      - Buys features: one author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website.
      - Needs: a strong claim.
    - Space admins
      - Adds: admins recorded per space, and powers that only they have, such as changing the space password, joining and leaving groups, and removing someone's access.
      - Buys security: each power given to admins is taken away from everyone who holds the space password.
      - Needs: a strong claim, or a co-member could claim the admin's account and become admin.
    - Device keys
      - Adds: each device where the plugin runs registers a key, and later claims must come from a registered device.
      - Buys security: prevents forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run, including people with no personal account.
      - Cost: people confirm each new device.
    - Proof from Roam's server
      - Adds: an optional proof using a Roam backend token, from one person or stored per graph by an admin.
      - Buys security: no forgery for the people it covers. It also proves who is an admin.
      - Cost: needs a Roam subscription. Storing tokens is expensive to do safely.
    - Proof from Roam's login
      - Adds: the plugin sends proof of who is logged in to Roam.
      - Buys security: no forgery for any Roam user, with no effort.
      - Blocked: Roam's terms of service and Roam's agreement. Unlikely.
    - Agents acting for a person
      - Adds: an agent reads what its person reads, as a restricted login of that person rather than a separate identity.
      - Buys features: the agent follows the person's reach as it grows.
    - Visibility settings
      - Adds: the person chooses what the public, each group, and people in shared spaces see of their profile.

- Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it
  - **Why it matters:** the rest of this page describes the long-term design. The first release of personal accounts will be much smaller: almost certainly no strong proof of identity, and probably nothing that depends on Roam's own login. This section says what that release contains, which steps can follow, and what each step buys in security or in features, so the group can choose the order.
  - "Accounts v0" means the first release of personal accounts. It is not the product v0, which is done.
  - Weak and strong claims
    - When a person connects a platform account from a plugin, they claim "this platform account is me".
    - In v0 every claim is weak: the only evidence is that it came from someone using that space. Any co-member could have made it.
    - A strong claim comes with a proof that a co-member can't fake. Each step below that adds a proof turns some weak claims into strong ones.
    - The question for each stage is how far a weak claim reaches, and what a co-member gains by forging one.
  - Proposed accounts v0
    - A person creates a Discourse Graphs account on the Website, with a password or a common social login such as Google or GitHub.
    - The person connects their platform account from the plugin, once per space, or more widely (see "Open: how far a weak claim reaches in v0").
    - The plugin keeps acting as the space for sync, groups and sharing. It acts as the person for reads and search.
    - Website: a banner that says who is signed in, and an account page that lists the connected platform accounts and the spaces they reach.
    - Plugins: an indicator of who the plugin acts as, a button to connect or reconnect, and search across the person's spaces.
    - Open: how the plugin gets the person's login. A one-time token handed from the plugin to the Website is the simplest. A standard login flow (OAuth) is the long-term leaning, but needs a consent page and more setup.
    - Not in v0: attribution, space admins, agents acting for a person, and visibility settings beyond "name shown, email hidden".
  - Open: how far a weak claim reaches in v0
    - Narrow: only the space where the claim was made.
      - A forger gains nothing: they already act as that space.
      - Cost: the person connects from each space before search covers it.
    - Wider, read-only: also every other space where the same platform account appears, for reading only.
      - The person connects once, and search covers all their spaces.
      - A forger can read the victim's other spaces. In Roam, a person often belongs to several graphs, so this is a real leak.
    - Wider, full: the same reach, with the same permissions the platform account has there.
      - A forger can act in the victim's other spaces.
    - Whatever v0 allows can tighten later, once strong claims exist: weak claims would fall back to a narrower reach. People then lose access they had, so a wider v0 reach should be announced as temporary.
  - What v0 buys
    - Search inside the plugins across the person's spaces, without creating a group just for that.
    - Login on the Website as a person, without going through a plugin.
    - People, not only spaces, as group admins.
    - Security: with the narrow reach, no change from today. With a wider reach, the leak described above.
  - What v0 still allows
    - Any co-member can claim another member's platform account. With the narrow reach they gain no access, but the account page shows them as that member.
    - Open: what happens when a second person claims an account that is already claimed. If the first claim wins, a co-member can block the real owner. If the newest claim wins, two people can take the account back and forth.
    - Names: a weak claim doesn't show who made it. If the claimant's profile name replaced the platform name, a co-member could rename another member's work. Until strong claims exist, v0 should keep showing the platform name.
  - Steps after v0
    - These can come in any order, except where a step names what it needs.
    - Notify and detect conflicts
      - Adds: a mail when an account is connected, a check when the plugin starts ("Was this you?"), and a hold on claims that conflict until someone settles them.
      - Buys security: a forged claim is noticed fast and can be reversed. It also gives a blocked owner a way out.
      - Needs: a verified email on the personal account.
    - Match the email
      - Adds: a claim becomes strong when the person's account controls the email that the platform records for the platform account.
      - Buys features: the claim reaches all the person's spaces at once. Attribution becomes possible.
      - Buys security: stops a co-member who can't fake the platform's email record.
      - Limit: Roam only, until we know whether Obsidian exposes a verified email.
    - Agreement between spaces
      - Adds: a claim becomes strong when two or more spaces recorded the same account details before the claim.
      - Buys features: the same wider reach, with no effort, for people in several graphs.
      - Buys security: stops a forger who shares only one graph with the victim.
    - Attribution
      - Adds: the person's chosen name on their work, attribution in the export, and verified identifiers such as ORCID.
      - Buys features: one author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website.
      - Needs: a strong claim.
    - Space admins
      - Adds: admins recorded per space, and powers that only they have, such as changing the space password, joining and leaving groups, and removing someone's access.
      - Buys security: each power given to admins is taken away from everyone who holds the space password.
      - Needs: a strong claim, or a co-member could claim the admin's account and become admin.
    - Device keys
      - Adds: each device where the plugin runs registers a key, and later claims must come from a registered device.
      - Buys security: prevents forgery against anyone whose plugin has already run, including people with no personal account.
      - Cost: people confirm each new device.
    - Proof from Roam's server
      - Adds: an optional proof using a Roam backend token, from one person or stored per graph by an admin.
      - Buys security: no forgery for the people it covers. It also proves who is an admin.
      - Cost: needs a Roam subscription. Storing tokens is expensive to do safely.
    - Proof from Roam's login
      - Adds: the plugin sends proof of who is logged in to Roam.
      - Buys security: no forgery for any Roam user, with no effort.
      - Blocked: Roam's terms of service and Roam's agreement. Unlikely.
    - Agents acting for a person
      - Adds: an agent reads what its person reads, as a restricted login of that person rather than a separate identity.
      - Buys features: the agent follows the person's reach as it grows.
    - Visibility settings
      - Adds: the person chooses what the public, each group, and people in shared spaces see of their profile.
      - Matters once attribution shows profile names.
    - Contributing from the Website
      - Adds: a personal space on the Website for proposed nodes, connected to published nodes.
